notes.content:
[p][/p][h3][b]Hello! [/b]ːsteamhappyː[/h3][p][/p][p]I can hardly believe it, but we’re finally here! This is the last public test update of [i][b]Echoes of the Community: The Major Overhaul[/b][/i]. The next update of this scale won’t be added to the public test branch. Instead, it will be included in the this huge update build we have and then pushed directly to the main Early Access branch as an official major update.[/p][p]It has been a tough journey, but the game has truly reached another level compared to the old main branch. With this update, that difference is really starting to shine on the player-facing side as well.[/p][p]The last update fixed the infamous freeze issue, but it also introduced a few new problems into the bug pipeline. This update also addresses those setbacks with lots of additional fixes. But while going back into the core systems, I also had the chance to improve a lot of things along the way: elevators, pathfinding, and how people interact with items. These were always planned for later, but they came earlier than expected. The overall flow of people, moving around with elevators, escalators, and stairs; feels so much smoother now. And with all the added polish like new animations, missing behaviors, and audio work, the game feels less “mechanical” and much more alive.[/p][p]Since I wasn’t able to deliver the planned weekend patch right after the last update, I decided to go the extra mile and add more polish this time, animations, balancing, and fixes, to make this the [b]final[/b] public test update before we migrate the build to the main branch. That way, Nil and I can fully focus on the final push toward the autumn event.[/p][p]What’s next after this update: finishing the tutorial, adding new decisions and achievements, refreshing the Steam page with new art and a trailer, some more polishing and remaning UI (main menu, QOL, etc.), and wrapping up everything needed for the main branch migration.[/p][p]Once this build is live on the main branch, the public test branch will close briefly, then reopen later for [b]Nightlife Update[/b] testing.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Highlights & Changelog[/b][/h3][p][b]— Major Pathfinding & Elevator Logic Improvements[/b] [/p][p]These pathfinding choice logic and elevator logic improvements have been on the list since the Early Access launch because they’re so important to how the simulation feels. In my view, people flow is one of the biggest parts of the late-game fun in a simulation game like this, and it’s frustrating to run into odd behavior when you’re carefully designing your tower.[/p][p]I’ve made tweaks here and there before, but this was the real overhaul, a big rewrite with new penalty systems for escalators, stairs, distances, and crowded elevators. The difference is huge compared to the old system. But now the foundation is now in place, Im sure we’ll keep tweaking as development continues.[/p][p][b]— Elevator Logic Overhaul[/b] Elevator behavior is now much closer to real life, especially in [i]Realistic[/i] mode. I also added four new elevator operating modes (plus full customization):[/p][list][*][p][b]Realistic[/b] – Standard modern elevator operation.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Simplified[/b] – Always takes the first request, stops for everyone.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Old Quirky[/b] – Outdated elevator style, feels random, stops everywhere.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Luxury/Express[/b] – Skips most calls, prioritizes top floors.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Custom[/b] – Fine-tune every behavior.[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/e63ec46cf6f1df214b295f2deea727291d7f9056.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]— “Now Go Up! Now Go Down!” & Elevator Line UI[/b] [/p][p]The elevator UI got a big design pass, plus a fun little feature: you can now manually send an elevator up or down, even for no reason at all. You can even flip its direction mid-ride. It’s surprisingly entertaining, and who knows, maybe we should add a full manual-control mini-game mode to it![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/0885abaae103ea0cc3f31908864e4061054da11a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]— People Coming & Going Both Ways[/b]
Another pathfinding update I’d like to mention: walkways now support people traveling in both directions. This was a highly requested polish feature. It was a bit challenging to implement in the old system because of how it handled tile data, but thanks to the rebuilt backend, it’s finally possible.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/07399ab13a03a338e55ef3a4a7069eb2c6f95273.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]— Pricing, Vending, and Prices Menu UI[/b]
The pricing menu was waiting for me to start the final UI polish pipeline, and since it was in a rough state, it was the first one on the list. I’ve updated its design and also removed vending options from inner room pricing. Having all possible vending items mixed into room pricing was causing a lot of confusion.[/p][p]My long-term plan for vending machines is that, after this major update (with the Nightlife Update), I’ll separate them fully from restaurant and café menus. They’ll get their own dedicated system and menu, with more items, billboard/advertising integration, and the option to either outsource their management for a cut or run and stock everything yourself, which is similar to how it works now.[/p][p]For the moment, vending is handled as its own system. The AI already treats it mostly separate from the room system, some vending types pull from inventories directly, others need menu items. Previously, though, vending prices were tied to the room they belonged to. This caused problems and weird situations where the same vending machines in different rooms had different prices. To fix that, vending and transportation services are now priced separately from room-based services and products.[/p][p]Also, people of different wealth types now judge the prices of transportation and vending based only on the overall casino resort rating, instead of factoring in the prestige level of the room they’re in.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/85bb62a5e12fe7b88fe8033bfe0fae49eb21d0d4.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3][b]The Polish Work Highlights[/b][/h3][p][b]— Animation & Audio FX Improvements[/b] [/p][p]The setbacks from the last update have been resolved, and lots of polish has been added. New animations and sound effects (idles, eating, etc.) bring more life to the game. People now play “animation series” depending on their jobs rather than switching abruptly. Missing AI behaviors were also filled in, massage therapists now move around during the theraphy, wash hands, hairdressers assist the people on hooded hairdryers, and so on.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/1da18874ea0266ff2f7a6b9beedf092427c331ba.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]— New World UI Indicators[/b] [/p][p]New hoverable indicators were added for resort services. For example, you can now see what’s happening in restaurants, orders being prepared, customer wait times, and more. Office workers also got animations and audio polish.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d60ce26779a6379c2ac3c49792d5e4e910270eb4.gif"][/img][/p][p][b]— Lamp Colors[/b]
You can finally change lamp colors! This was originally planned for Nightlife, but it’s been requested for over a year, so I decided to sneak it in now. Some colors look fantastic with certain wallpapers. It’s not full 3D lighting, but for a 2D game it goes a long way.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/265e48fee795cf877fcf8b54d974066f9d651d76.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]— New Cars & Dirt Variations[/b]
AI-owned vehicles now include new types and dirt/maintenance variations. These visuals tie in nicely with the new garage mechanics.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/da470ec943d54de4801e0dc980d5ed95d07f4ffe.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]— New Escalator & Item Variations[/b]
A couple of new visual escalator variations have been added. The long-term plan (coming with Nightlife) is to let you upgrade elevator parts and escalator speeds indefinitely, with visual options to match.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/e3e91ed31502e5e85fd6798276ed33ebec5f82bb.gif"][/img][/p][p]— [b]Builder Headlights and Gear[/b][/p][p]The builders’ hats now emit light, and Nil also created some visual varieties for the boxes they place in the construction area. Lots of cool additions are planned for the tower construction side of the game with the [i]Architecting Heights[/i] update, which will be released after the [i]Nightlife[/i] update.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]The Changelog[/b][/h3][p][b]Fixes / Improvements[/b][/p][list][*][p]Receptionists and dealers now play more varied animations while working.[/p][/*][*][p]Added audio FX to hair salon AI actions.[/p][/*][*][p]Hair dryer is now used by guests in the hair salon and also by hairdressers while assisting them as part of their work.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the issue of smoking cigar animation causing graphic glitches on face expressions.[/p][/*][*][p]Added new audio varieties to the dice games.[/p][/*][*][p]Added new audio varieties to the casino cashiers and reception desks.[/p][/*][*][p]You can now change the color of the lamps in your casino resort; It usually showed up right on the hour and felt completely random. I found possible causes and patched them, but the freeze kept coming back. In the end it required a base level refactor, and after days of debugging and writing unit tests, I finally tracked down the real issue.[/p][p]It was not really about lawsuits or decision popups, even though it often looked that way. The actual problem was tied to player state changes such as placing items, stairs, elevator shafts, making decisions, assigning casino games, end of day reports, or any transition that paused the game. The tricky part was that it only triggered if that state change happened during a single low FPS frame. That is why it seemed random and why some players hit it more often than others, since it even depended on PC performance and what else their computer was doing at the time.[/p][p]CRT does not use the engine’s built in physics since it is too heavy for a sim, and instead uses math libraries for collision checks in placement, selection, vehicle traffic, and more. The bug was buried in how the game handled this simulation while paused and in certain states. That is why all our tests on lawsuits, decisions, and spawns never revealed it, because the real problem was deeper in the underlying system.[/p][p]It was a nightmare to track down, but it feels amazing to be sure it is finally gone before merging into the main branch. There is no way I could have greenlit launch with it still in place.[/p][p]With this fixed I can finally shift back to balance, smaller to mid level fixes, QOL, and polishing. The refactor caused a few new bugs with state changes and overlays, but most of those are already resolved. notes.title: [Public Test Update] v0.7.5.0.75 (pt)
notes.content:
[p][b]Hello![/b] ːsteamhappyː[/p][p][/p][p]I released an update to the public test branch yesterday, but it was around 11 PM here and I was pretty exhausted. So I’m writing this log now in the morning here in Bangkok. I’ve decided to turn this into a full public test branch update log after two smaller patches. I’ve mostly been quiet on the daily quick devlogs, only chatting on Discord, the Steam Community Hub, and in bug report discussions. That time has been spent moving forward with the plans we’ve already talked about in earlier update logs and devlogs for this final polishing phase of the update, which at this point feels almost like a second early access launch. [/p][p]This update brings in previously missing items that were only listed in the item menu, more polished AI behaviors, UI improvements, final tweaks before we start the real money and documents balancing, and, of course, some important fixes, like the massive save file sizes in mid to late game and the long saving times caused by large financial data. Working on these issues also led me to improve the entire loading and game startup systems. [/p][p][/p][p]Here are some highlights from this update, followed by the full changelog:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d39f0fb33288af083b2692929b697242579ec1fd.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Missing Items and AI Behaviors[/b] [/p][p]Added the previously missing new vending items that were only listed in the items menu but were nonfunctional and unresearcheable. These include the pipe vending stand, lighter vending stand, condom vending machine, and period product vending machine, along with their related inventory items for buying and storing. I also added the research options for these items and reintroduced the benches to the research tree. Their AI usage has also been implemented, these are the first batch of polish-like AI behaviors and animations I mentioned last week. There are still more to complete, which I plan to finish this week. [/p][p]The condom and period product vending machines are now required for prestige-level items in restrooms, while the pipe and lighter vending stands are now prestige-level needs in cigar lounges. I’ve added these items now since they were already planned and I was already working on implementing them. All room prestige-level requirements and bonuses will get some love this week, and any missing ones will be completed. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/38aed95e8b0e46f1b653f6c2f6fe177045cc3f6b.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]UI and QOL Changes and Improvements[/b] [/p][p]I’ve made some progress on UI polishing and quality-of-life improvements. I updated the design and tab system logic across the side information menus for items, customers, employees, and rooms. Now all side tab buttons are fully incorporated into the menus and serve both as info displays and toggles for more detailed information. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d939c1afdd7ef9f58ad18781c9c38004a2b0b226.jpg"][/img][/p][p]I also made some edits to the leisure research tree while implementing the missing polish-like side items. The event and meeting room research options are temporarily removed. They will be added back with the Nightlife update as part of its new calendar and organization/events features. [/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/3e4bb9b65752da68e870553d8830535283bae0e5.jpg"][/img][/p][p][b]Startup & Loading System[/b] [/p][p]Last week, Nil and some community players mentioned that save times were long, and I noticed some bloated financial data. I refactored and improved the system, which massively reduced the data size. I also shortened the number of collected days from 15 to 7, which also makes the financial data graphs cleaner and easier to understand. [/p][p]As the game is becoming a proper simulation and with even more features coming, I decided to improve the save loading and startup systems as well. Now, when the game starts, it only loads one save per casino resort you have. Later, when you navigate the saved games menu, the other saves load asynchronously, so you don’t have to wait for all the casino saves to load before the menu opens. [/p][p]I’ll also be polishing the UI design of it while finishing up the remaining main menu work.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Employees & Balancing[/b] [/p][p]We will start working on the proper balance of the economy, both money and administrative documents, especially on the transportation side tomorrow. That said, I have been making small adjustments to the balancing system as planned. [/p][p]One key change is how employee quitting works. Instead of recalculating the chance to quit every day, it now accumulates over time: [/p][p]• Unhappy workers slowly build up their quit chance each day. 
 • Happy workers gradually reduce their accumulated quit chance. 
 • Employees only start considering quitting once their chance reaches 40 percent. [/p][p][/p][list][*][p][i]Formula (for the curious):[/i] 
 chanceToQuit = chanceToQuit + (10 - 2.5f * jobHappiness) [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][i]Examples:[/i] 
 jobHappiness = 0 → 10 
 jobHappiness = 4 → 0 
 jobHappiness = 6 → -5 
 jobHappiness = 8 → -10 
 jobHappiness = 10 → -15 (plus the HR manager boost) [/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]In short, the happier your employees are, the more their quit chance heals over time. [/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]Some Other News[/b] [/p][p]Since we’re back to frequent mid-sized updates and patches, there aren’t long silences between updates anymore like there used to be during the early beta testing days of this rework. With that, I want to adjust how I handle posts and logs again. Quick short devlogs were great, but when I’m buried in heavy work, they eat up a lot of time. And since I don’t want to flood the Steam news feed, I try to sneak them in creatively here and there :) [/p][p]Here’s what I’m planning for communication going forward: [/p][list][*][p][i]On Steam[/i] 
 I’ll be posting dev news in update logs like this, now that updates are coming every one to two weeks again. Patch notes will stay as simple changelogs, and more detailed future plans will go into the Community Gazette alongside major update logs. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][i]On Reddit[/i] 
 I plan to unpin the devlog thread and start posting update logs, Community Gazettes, and major updates as standalone posts. Smaller patch notes and quick devlog-style updates will go into the comments of those posts on Steam. I also found out I can enable images in comments through the mod tools, which I thought wasn’t possible because the subreddit is new. I’m still learning subreddit management, so thank you for bearing with me. [/p][/*][/list][list][*][p][i]On Discord[/i] 
 I use announcements to share every link I post to Steam, but I only ping everyone for major news. If you want to catch everything, you’ll need to keep an eye on it. I also post smaller work-in-progress notes in the devlog channel, and these update logs will go there too. As always, I keep an eye on feedback and bug reports and respond when I can. [/p][/*][/list][p]Outside of that, as you probably know if you’ve been following the development closely, I’m always around to chat and bounce ideas on the CRT Subreddit, Steam Community Hub, and Discord channels.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][b]The Changelog[/b][/p][p][b]Fixes[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where the changed number of contracted delivery people wasn’t being sent by the delivery company until the next delivery time.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some customers could book rooms without paying.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed gumball and keychain machines not consuming the related inventory items.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where people standing in item lines weren’t saved correctly, causing them to leave after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a rare issue where customers could leave the café while their order was still being prepared.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the CEO sometimes wouldn’t show up to work or would leave immediately.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some abandoned cars weren’t marked as abandoned, keeping their driver data in the vehicle information menu and causing issues.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where builders would leave after finishing their work, leaving one behind. When a new job arrived, they wouldn’t return because one was still counted as active and the truck didn’t depart.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the tow truck could get stuck at the entrance, causing the system to keep spawning cars and tow trucks just outside the map, leading to lag near the edge of the map.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where passengers wouldn’t board a bus for a long time, causing delays for others and the bus itself.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where save files wouldn’t load if they contained a driver unable to reach their car due to a pathfinding problem.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where worker trucks displayed "getting towed" information in the vehicle information menu incorrectly.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where guests could line up for casino game items disabled by the player.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where detained suspects spawned on the elevator entrance floor if the game was saved while they were in the elevator with an without apprehending a suspect, causing suspects to leave the detention cell.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where keychain machines didn’t generate demand for keychains in the inventory menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the employee side info menu didn’t sync break schedules after closing the assignment pop-up menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where suspects continued their walking animations on escalators while under arrest.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed rendering issues with some subway train parts on the map.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where inventory items weren’t displayed correctly on storage shelves after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed room menu financial reports not syncing correctly.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the favorites box not showing the customer service notes.title: [Public Test Update] v0.7.5.0.71 (pt)
notes.content: [p][/p][p]Hey everyone! ːsteamhappyː[/p][p][/p][p]After a round of patches, I’ve finally jumped into the last remaining system we hadn’t reworked yet over the last week: the Townsfolk system. It feels great to finally be at this point. Aside from the tutorial, polish, and ongoing fixes, this was the final big piece left. Since Echoes of the Community was all about revisiting and rebuilding older systems and adding community most-wanted mechanics, it only made sense to include Townsfolk in that too. I mean, why not make this update wait even longer and rework every single thing while Steam kind of shouts at me “upload this thing to the main branch already!” [/p][p]But seriously, this rework was long overdue. With the new systems where Townsfolk are now needed to get city licenses and expand transport capacity, they’ve become more important than ever. So fixing quest issues, adding new mechanics, and improving the UI felt like the right final step.[/p][p][/p][p]Also packed into this update are a bunch of improvements to employee breaks, utilities, audio mixing, and more. I was originally planning to push a couple more patches just for fixes before starting Townsfolk, but I ended up using that time to go all in, so everything’s bundled into this one.[/p][p][/p][p]So here are the highlights and the changelog:[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]Townsfolk Backstories & Character[/h3][p]Each Townsfolk character now has a new little backstory, and I’ve tried to make quest texts reflect their personalities instead of being cold and robotic like “Place X items” only text. These little touches should make them feel more like actual residents of your city, not just quest givers. They also now have unique mumble voice lines, like our beloved casino guy.[/p][p]We're planning to share a Google Form soon if you'd like to help write backstories for them! These little lore-like details will tie into future updates like [b]Rivalries[/b] and [b]Celebrities & Press[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/aaf61d7cc87bfd0655eeddeaf6b1470a52112b41.jpg"][/img][/p][h3]Townsfolk Corruption & Gifts[/h3][p]Besides the tasks they give (which you can now request manually as well), there was a system where you could give gifts or ask for money to affect your relationship. Now, each Townsfolk character has a corruption value, which can sometimes change through sending persuasive documents and with some events.. If a Townsfolk is highly corrupt, gifts are more likely to work. If not, trying to bribe them might result in a lawsuit or a hit to your rating. You can now also manually request tasks from them, which helps reduce randomness and gives you a bit more control over what you’re working toward.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/95096d56ed62022ab2da5bd8bd1942043a6561b4.gif"][/img][/p][h3]Employee Breaks[/h3][p]While working on bugs related to staff break room selection and time issues, I also found myself working on the “couldn’t find break room item” animation. That was supposed to be part of the polish pass next week, but I couldn’t help myself after seeing the protest boards Nil drew.  Now employees go on little strikes if they can’t get the items they want. Also removed the possibility for armchairs, sofas, and dining tables to be favorite employee items (since they’re common helper items that every employee prefers to use if available, and were causing issues) and added items like yoga mats, gaming PCs, and exercise balls instead. New candidates are now also much more likely to want items you’ve already researched.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/21fc80e6a35710fa6f97624426e0bde3b7a02ab6.gif"][/img][/p][h3]Utility Async[/h3][p]Ive also made the electricity system async, and also added little animations to lamps when power comes or goes. This all started while fixing the crash ⁠related to a utility line calculations. While working on it, I figured it was a good chance to make the system more flexible, now we can also support stuff like circuit breakers or delays before power shuts off for future updates. On top of that, I removed the production prestige bonus from utility rooms, as it was causing a loop where a power shortage would lower prestige, which would then lower production, leading to even more shortages. The info text is still outdated for now, but I’ll be revisiting room prestige in general later this week, so that’ll be updated with the new buffs and tooltips.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/09c7eb73eb09812cec947ad3a947ef0df41c2e95.png"][/img][/p][h3]Delivery and Waste Collection Hours[/h3][p]There were also fixes related to delivery and waste collection. Previously, delivery personnel wouldn’t leave if they couldn’t keep up with demand, and waste collectors would sometimes collect all dumpster trash in one go. Now, delivery and collection workers have proper hours. Deliveries happen between 7–10 and 19–22, while waste collection runs between 4–6 and 16–18. When their shift ends, they leave. This should help make it more obvious when you need to contract more workers for those specific times, rather than assuming it’s a bug or a stuck worker.[/p][p][/p][h3]Audio Mixing and Balancing[/h3][p]The audio system has finally started receiving some attention too. While working on Townsfolk voice lines, I ended up doing a first pass on audio mixing. The old crowd ambiance was creating a weird “video-like” constant background noise, so I blended that out and bumped up the casino audio effects. More importantly, I started tuning the spatial blend, distance, and doppler values of audio sources so that sounds better reflect your camera position. Ambience should now fade out more cleanly, and the overall soundscape should feel more alive and dynamic. There’s still more work to do in this area, but this was a necessary first step. As of this week, I’ll also be starting on the full balancing pass for document production/usage, and the pricing and cost systems, now that Townsfolk is finally off the task list.[/p][p]I already feel like the game is starting to sound and feel more alive, and that will only get better from here.[/p][p][/p][p]Lastly, I’m planning to write a Community Gazette this week to go over the current release stage and the updated roadmap. I’ll share more details there on what’s coming next and how we’re planning to approach it.[/p][p][/p][p]I'm now officially down to mostly polish-level fixes according to the bug pipeline, which feels like a big milestone after all the major reworks.[/p][p]But there's still that one infamous issue left, the hour start freeze bug. It happens rarely, but when it does, it's frustrating. I've tried a lot of profiling and different approaches, but couldn't pin it down in time for this update.[/p][p]The good news is, I finally have a save file where it shows up more consistently, about once every 15 to 20 loads, so I'm hoping that helps me finally track it down and fix it with this week's patches.[/p][p]If you're encountering it more frequently, please feel free to send over a save notes.title: [Public Test Patch] v0.7.5.0.64 (pt)
notes.content: [p]Hello! Patch [b]v0.7.5.0.64[/b] is now live on the [b]Public Test Branch[/b]! Here’s the changelog, along with some notes I also mentioned in the last [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1457030/discussions/5/"]dev-diary[/url]:[/p][p][/p][p]As you’ve probably noticed from the recent patches, I’m still working through the last of the transportation system fixes. Unlocking the subway turned out to be like opening a beehive. I didn’t expect it to touch so many things, but since transportation is connected to the spawning system, and that’s tied to almost all core systems, every change ripples out. Since the public test build is almost identical to the development build right now, I know it’s not exactly fun to play while I mess with core systems like this, but I hope this patch will really put us past the toughest parts.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Subway Train Improvements[/b] [/p][p]While working on the subway issues, I also made some changes to how the train behaves. As you keep adding wagons and the train gets longer, wagons outside the subway stop’s range weren’t unloading passengers properly. Now the train will move and stop for each wagon so they unload properly at the center of the station. After (hopefully) wrapping up the townsfolk this weekend and moving more into the polishing phase, I’ll also be adding a bunch of fun details, like subway tracks on the train floor, metallic particles and sparks when it stops, and other little touches to bring more life and atmosphere. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Changelog:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Fixed an issue where subway trains would arrive missing wagons or not arrive at all after maintenance.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved a bug where customers were added to the bus passenger list before actually arriving at the bus station.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where customers, after getting tired from climbing stairs, would respawn back at the map entrance.[/p][/*][*][p]Employees now no longer receive a "Had to cut visit short." negative moodlet or cut visits short due to excessive stair climbing.[/p][/*][*][p]Selling a locomotive while it's still on the map no longer causes issues.[/p][/*][*][p]Parked vehicle colliders (builder trucks, police cars, garbage trucks) now sync correctly after loading the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved issue where locomotive drivers were fired after selling a wagon.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed incorrect tooltip text on the sell button in the garage vehicle menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Garage vehicle passenger lists no longer scroll to the top every few seconds.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed the prestige piano item from the Mexican Cantina, Italian Ristorante, and French Bistro. This was left in mistakenly and will return with the Nightlife update.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed customers not entering the jackpot win state when they should.[/p][/*][*][p]Disabled items no longer become re-enabled after reloading the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed glitch that could occur on the main menu if there was a loading issue.[/p][/*][*][p]Game no longer gets stuck during loading when owning an Expressline Haul engine with more than 8 passengers.[/p][/*][*][p]Taxi queuing per owned taxi reduced from 5 to 3.[/p][/*][*][p]Taxis now line up correctly when waiting for others to finish unloading passengers.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed pathfinding error causing vehicles to wait for others even when no vehicle is in front of them.[/p][/*][*][p]Subway wagons no longer leave passengers behind if the locomotive departs.[/p][/*][*][p]Subway trains now correctly stop and unload passengers at each wagon along long platforms, instead of teleporting them to the station.[/p][/*][*][p]People waiting for the subway in a saved game no longer disappear after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Crimes with unassigned police officers no longer cause loading issues.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed passengers trying to "reach" subway trains or bus doors even when they were already at the entrance.[/p][/*][*][p]Researching "Cafe Service" now also unlocks the dish cleaning station and waiters.[/p][/*][*][p]Passengers no longer continue waiting at stations for vehicles that have been sold.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed maintenance vehicle scroll bar issue where the maintenance box wouldn’t respond.[/p][/*][*][p]People in subway wagons will now remain inside if the locomotive is undergoing maintenance.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where people at the casino hotel kept waiting for wagons without a functioning locomotive.[/p][/*][*][p]Mechanics now properly auto-start pending multiple maintenance tasks depending on their skill level.[/p][/*][*][p]Velvetline and Comfortline wagons no longer render as basic transit wagons.[/p][/*][*][p]Wagons no longer remain in a "no driver" state after their locomotive is sold and re-bought.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved an error that caused patrol routes to treat their assigned base rooms as closed, even when they were open.[/p][/*][*][p]Added the missing moodlet effect for the employee restroom.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where customers were sometimes checking the wrong car data list, causing performance issues.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved a bug where the garage vehicle info menu attempted to display information for a sold vehicle.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed visual glitches in the subway menu’s passenger list.[/p][/*][*][p]Subway train scroll in the subway menu no longer gets stuck in one position.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]I'll see you in the next one![/b] It’ll likely focus more on townsfolk updates, alongside the beginning of polish, audio mixing and balance improvements. Bug fixes are still on the way too, there are a more to tackle before this becomes a clean default branch update. Feels like we’ve got some solid momentum going now, so let’s finish this up in no time![/p][p][/p][p]As always, thank you so much for your support through all of this. It truly means a lot. ❤️[/p]

notes.content: [p][b]Hello! [/b][/p][p][/p][p]Since the last update, I’ve mostly been focusing on fixes and improvements, and I think we’ve finally reached the point where there are no more game-breaking crashes, which is a huge relief. There are still a bunch of small to mid-sized bugs hiding here and there, but hopefully, this update will clean up a good portion of them. After this patch I’ll also start shifting focus toward all the missing polish-style AI behaviors and item interactions to help make the game feel much smoother overall.[/p][p]This will include things like spending time in different areas, new sitting and idle animations, waiting in line animations, usage of helper items such as using hair dryers at the hairdresser, waiting for public transport, and interacting with the new vending machines, including those for condoms, period products, and pipe & lighter.[/p][p][/p][p]To really get things in order, I’ve also been revisiting the entire system and collecting a lot of data for balancing. Nil has been a huge help during this process, she created isolated save files for each major system, which has made testing way more manageable and honestly saved me from getting overwhelmed.[/p][p][/p][p]I’ve also worked on some QOL and balance-related features and improvements. Here are some highlights from this update:[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/0b92aa66676d066967a76e3074ca879bc028aa88.gif"][/img][/p][h3][b]Merged Utility Connector Removal[/b][/h3][p]Since we introduced switchboards, it’s become clear that redesigning utility layouts (cables, tubes, etc.) can be a huge pain. So I’ve now merged the removal tools for regular and bridge connectors. That means you can now use the same tool to mass-remove all connectors in a selected area. Much smoother![/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/5dcdcd324b4f3b6b2e702e4797f28601fc596520.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]New Item: CCTV Server[/b][/h3][p]Late-game saves were starting to look like monitoring table factories, way too many of them. This new item should help a lot: the CCTV Server takes up much less space, has higher capacity, and will eventually be paired with changes that make regular monitoring tables require staffed security guards. These servers, however, will work independently.[/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/dbc64c447ada91f367b4b4263d5a8c04029a49b4.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Storage Shelf Stacking[/b][/h3][p]Another issue I noticed was storage shelf sprawl. As we add more inventory items (and I have no plans to stop doing that 😄), space becomes a problem. So I’ve added two new research options that let you upgrade your placed storage item capacity to 2x and 3x. Space saved![/p][p][/p][p][/p][h3]🛠️[b]Bug Fixes[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Fixed a bug causing incoming people to become stuck in broken vehicles waiting for maintenance.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved a rare crash where AI script tried to access floor data before floors were initialized.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where humans synced colliders while hover data was null.[/p][/*][*][p]Hotel payments are now made [b]after usage[/b], instead of during the booking.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where escalator info boxes would return null during loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Customers now correctly leave after using the mini bar in hotel rooms.[/p][/*][*][p]Garage runner no longer keeps vehicle data between sessions after a reload.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a bug where current settings would become null if the save file used for loading was deleted.[/p][/*][*][p]Bus stops now properly sync after a bus completes maintenance.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved visual glitch with escalator electricity error graphics.[/p][/*][*][p]Bridge connector removal now also removes the connected bridge (merged logic).[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed electricity line surplus calculation errors after loading a game with placed switchboards.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed "Buy Taxi" button showing incorrect tooltip for bus purchases.[/p][/*][*][p]Waste collector icons no longer appear incorrectly as police icons.[/p][/*][*][p]Annoying employee stranded notifications have been improved.[/p][/*][*][p]Toilet papers now get consumed properly as intended. (Might need some balance though)[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where customers from older save files would remain idle.[/p][/*][*][p]Elevator electricity errors now correctly trigger info boxes.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved bug causing customers to get stuck in the "use restaurant" state.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed switchboards not connecting items properly after rooms are merged.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bug causing garage vehicle sale list to grow infinitely.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced loading time for item data.[/p][/*][*][p]Achievements menu no longer updates while closed.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where previously earned achievements would reappear after loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Walkways menu now shows the correct stamp and dont start a survay again after authorizing construction.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where people were waiting for garage vehicles even if they were broken or in maintenance.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved the bug causing the taxi rank to display "no taxi" error even when a taxi was present in the garage.[/p][/*][*][p]Walkways menu button now properly displays "Not enough money" error.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed unnecessary, repetitive pathfinding calculations during game loading.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed missing moodlets for: Executive Office, Yoga Studio, Smoothie Bar, Asian Fusion Restaurant, Cyber Cafe, Steakhouse, and several other rooms.[/p][/*][*][p]Customers from older save files no longer encounter null bus stop issues.[/p][/*][*][p]Room data now resets correctly when reloading a save from the escape menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where negotiation willingness slider text didn’t reflect the slider value.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where CCTV modules scaled excessively on hover while in demolish mode.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some buttons wouldn't play their animations while the game is paused.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the original room turning into a hall after placing a cloned room.[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved an issue where police officers incorrectly displayed stranded waste collector info in their popup info bar.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]⚖️[b]Some balance tweaks and improvements:[/b][/h3][list][*][p]Hotel base prices have been increased.[/p][/*][*][p]Public transport waiting logic improved: customers will now only wait if a scheduled vehicle is arriving within 2 hours (was 3).[/p][/*][*][p]Manager Mode starting money increased to [b]$500K[/b] and No Sweat Mode starting money increased to [b]$5M[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Storage shelf capacity can now be increased through the new [i]Stackin'[/i] researchs.[/p][/*][*][p]Burglar Alarm security increased from [b]8 → 15[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Safety Box security increased from [b]7 → 15[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Balance adjustments made to employee offer acceptance calculations.[/p][/*][*][p]Added modifier info boxes to the employee hiring window.[/p][/*][*][p]Employee hiring willingness is now correctly calculated between [b]0–100[/b] instead of [b]0–10[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][/p][p]I really feel like things have already started moving faster thanks to all the work we’ve done, yay! 😊[/p][p][/p][p]After some more fixes and improvements, we’ll start wrapping everything up with the more fun and visible stuff like the new townsfolk UI and quest system, the rest of the audio effects and mixing, more balancing passes, the updated tutorial, and finally the new achievements. I believe we’ll be able to release this before the end of the month, but we’ll see how things go.[/p][p][/p][p]Huge thanks to everyone for the reports, suggestions, and all the support.[/p][p]See you in the next one![/p][p]Cheers![/p]

notes.title: [Public Test Update] v0.7.5.0.53 (pt)
notes.content:
[p][b]Hey everyone![/b][/p][p][/p][p]This week marks the start of our new official [b]devlog series[/b]![/p][p]As some of you know, I’ve wanted to start a proper devlog for a while now, especially as we enter this more refined stage of our Early Access journey. During the big rework phase, most of the updates were shared in our Discord dev-diary channel, the Community Gazette, and through patch notes, but not always in a consistent, diary-like format. Things were evolving quickly, and it wasn’t always easy to keep up with everything in one place.[/p][p][/p][p]Now that the major rework is mostly behind us and development is entering a steadier rhythm, it feels like the perfect time to introduce a proper dev-diary![/p][p]These devlogs are now being shared in [b]three places[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]A new [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1457030/discussions/5/"]Devlog subforum[/url] in the [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/1457030/discussions/"]Steam Community Hub[/url][/p][/*][*][p]A centralized devlog thread on [url="https://www.reddit.com/r/CasinoResortTower/"]Reddit[/url][/p][/*][*][p]The usual [url="https://discord.com/channels/795947972021321728/1245947038022111232"]Discord dev-diary channel[/url][/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]It’s a great way to keep everyone in the loop, and honestly, it also helps me stay organized and track our progress more effectively. Plus, having a consistent running log will make putting together future Community Gazettes and patch notes much easier.[/p][p][/p][p]So with that said, let’s dive into the latest changelog!
But first, a big [b]thank you[/b] to everyone who’s been following along, testing, and sending in feedback. Your reports have directly shaped many parts of this update![/p][p][/p][h3]🛠️ Major Fixes & Improvements[/h3][p][/p][p]🚍 Transportation & Garage Maintenance[/p][list][*][p]Fixed UI scroll render glitch for [b]“pending”[/b] and [b]“in maintenance”[/b] vehicles.[/p][/*][*][p]Solved issue where scroll background icons displayed [b]above UI elements[/b] in taxi, bus, and subway menus.[/p][/*][*][p]Garage vehicle buttons now also display the [b]“No Driver”[/b] error box alongside maintenance warnings.[/p][/*][*][p]Vehicles now correctly [b]resume operations[/b] after being maintained.[/p][/*][*][p]Mechanics now [b]auto-start vehicle maintenance[/b] tasks properly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Mechanic skill level[/b] now reduces [b]maintenance time[/b] as expected.[/p][/*][*][p]Garage vehicles now [b]consume fuel[/b] and correctly [b]spend gas money[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Driver skill[/b] now affects [b]maintenance interval durations[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Vehicles in maintenance now [b]load correctly[/b] at game start.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed [b]vehicle maintenance slider[/b] issue in the UI.[/p][/*][*][p]Garage vehicles now contribute to [b]transport capacity calculations[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Subway menu now shows [b]total train fuel cost[/b] accurately.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed outdated [b]ticket price display[/b] from the subway menu.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Taxi and bus capacity[/b] now correctly affects transportation stats.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Subway usage stats[/b] now appear correctly in the end-of-day menu.[/p][/*][*][p]Walkway usage now displays accurate [b]hourly and daily data[/b].[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/61ee47e86b08046e828006418fa4851ad510bdfc.gif"][/img][/p][/*][/list][p]📊 Financial System & Graphs[/p][list][*][p]Major overhaul of the [b]financial graph[/b] and [b]data recording system[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Graphs now update [b]live[/b] and include [b]current-day data[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Resolved issue where [b]0-value transactions[/b] (e.g., “0 casino payback”) cluttered the system and skewed totals.[/p][/*][*][p]Removed phantom zero values at the start of a new game session.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed incorrect highlighting on [b]graph filter buttons[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Icons and headers now match their [b]corresponding transaction types[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Sub-graphs and main financial graphs are now [b]independently selectable[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where null icons caused totals to display [b]-100 million[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]⚠️ [i]This patch resets old financial logs for compatibility.[/i][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/6f2eacfd0ce2269953a8219405c938d424ad1c54.png"][/img][/p][p]🏨 Hotel Booking & Customer Behavior[/p][list][*][p]Customers now [b]explore and use vending machines[/b] if other options are unavailable.[/p][/*][*][p]Customers now wait in line for an employee if no one is currently available to provide service.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced [b]negative impact[/b] of "visit cut short" moodlets by [b]50%[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issue where customers [b]booked non-researched hotel rooms[/b] and immediately left.[/p][/*][*][p]Customers are now [b]less likely to want[/b] services you don’t have, even if researched.[/p][/*][*][p]Casino Cage moodlets now [b]correctly apply[/b] to customer mood.[/p][/*][*][p]Office moodlets now properly affect [b]employee mood[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed bug where customers would keep queueing at [b]empty vending machines[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Guests no longer leave immediately if there's no available [b]hotel room or casino cashier[/b].[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]📈 Reports, UI & Stats[/p][list][*][p][b]Taxi and bus guests[/b] now show up in the [b]end-of-day report[/b].[/p][/*][*][p][b]Visited employee count[/b] is now displayed accurately.[/p][/*][*][p]End-of-day menu now correctly includes [b]walkway-only transportation capacity[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Transport capacity is now calculated across all schedules—not just morning.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Traffic data reset[/b] for accurate recalibration.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a UI bug where certain [b]rating graph subs[/b] were shown incorrectly.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Rating graph redesign[/b] with cleaner display and live updates.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][p][/p][h3]⚖️ Balance Adjustments[/h3][list][*][p][b]Customers now arrive in greater numbers during peak hours (17:00–23:00).[/b][/p][p]This will play a much bigger role in the gameplay moving forward, especially with the upcoming [b]Nightlife Update’s Calendar System[/b] and the [b]Seasons Update[/b], which introduces seasonal mechanics. You’ll start to feel a more noticeable difference between evening and morning traffic, particularly as we begin balancing things further this week.[/p][p][/p][/*][*][p]Increased [b]daily service capacity contributions[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Hospitality: +25%[/p][/*][*][p]Cuisine: +50%[/p][/*][*][p]Leisure: +50%[/p][/*][*][p]Entertainment: +60%[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p][b]Base walkway capacity[/b] per level increased.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Upgrade costs[/b] for walkways lowered (base cost & growth factor).[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]I’m hoping to focus more on balance and polish later this week, once a few more fixes are out of the way. ːsteamhappyː[/p][p][/p][hr][/hr][p][/p][p][/p][h3]🎨 Art & Visuals[/h3][p]8 new wallpapers from the upcoming [b]Nightlife Update[/b] added early thanks to Nil’s extra time this week.[/p][p]
[/p][hr][/hr][p]
[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you all again for playing, reporting, and sticking with the game! Can’t wait to share more soon. This little game truly becoming something unique[/p][p][/p][p]Cheers![/p]

notes.title: [Public Test Update] Echoes Of The Community Update is Now in Beta!
notes.content:
[p][b]After a full year in the making, the massive update I’ve been working on is finally in its last stage of testing, focused on fixing, balancing, and polishing.[/b] What started as a public test build has now officially become the beta for what I’m calling the second "Early Access launch".[/p][p][/p][p][b]Would you play an early access of an early access game? [/b]ːsteammockingːːsteamhappyː[/p][p]This is by far the biggest update yet. The whole game has been [i]basically rebuilt from the ground up.[/i] Almost everything under the hood has been rewritten to be more stable, flexible, and future-proof. After launch, the scope of the game grew way beyond the original plans, so this update had to grow with it. Now, it’s finally ready for the long haul.[/p][p][/p][p]And the best part? It’s been completely shaped by the community. Every piece of feedback, every bug report, suggestion, wild idea, and late-night rant helped mold what this version became. So really, almost every feature we’ve agreed on together is in it.[/p][p][/p][p]So yeah, the main features are in, the new foundation is solid, and things are finally coming together. We’re almost there, and just about to kick off the huge roadmap ahead, packed with major updates and more content. But before all that, I could really use your help for one final round of testing on this upcoming unusually big update.[/p][p][/p][p]You can switch to the public test branch and jump in right now![/p][p][/p][p]⚠️ [b]Heads-up:[/b] There’s no tutorial yet. So if you’re brand new to the game, I recommend checking out the older version first to get the hang of it. (That tutorial wasn’t the best either, but hey, the new campaign mode and tutorial system are on the way!)[/p][p][/p][p]Things are still a bit rough:[/p][p]Some content is missing, the balance is all over the place, polish is... let’s just say “a work in progress,” and yes, there are definitely still bugs hiding in the corners. So if you’re just looking for a smooth and stable [i]Casino Resort Tower[/i] experience, I’d recommend waiting for the main branch release.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Thanks to this new foundation, updates from here on out will be and is much faster and smoother.[/b][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/4eea1bb82cdbc2f651a405ee2e2bba4632c2a791.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][h3]How to Switch to the Public Test Branch[/h3][olist][*][p]Open your [b]Steam Library[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Right-click on [b]Casino Resort Tower[/b] and select [b]Properties[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Go to the [b]Betas[/b] tab on the left[/p][/*][*][p]In the dropdown menu, select: [b]publictest - Public Test Branch[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Close the window, Steam will download the update automatically[/p][/*][*][p]Hit [b]Play[/b] when it’s ready and enjoy the test build![/p][/*][/olist][p][/p][p][/p][p]💡 [b]Bonus Tip for Testers:[/b][/p][p]Some of the [b]development tools[/b] are still available for now to help you quickly test things, since game balance isn’t fully in place yet.[/p][p]You can access them by pressing [b]O + P[/b] in-game.
[/p][p][/p][p]📢 [b]Update Logs & Community Posts:[/b]
I’m planning to share [b]regular update logs right here on Steam for the public test branch[/b], which will always stay active and maintain the next major update.[/p][p]This means there will be [b]three types of posts[/b] going forward:[/p][list][*][p][b]Public Test Branch Updates/Changelogs[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Main Branch Updates/Changelogs[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Community Gazette[/b]: where we’ll talk about future plans and community topics[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Looking forward to keeping you all in the loop and hearing your feedback! Thank you so much for being here. Let’s make this final stretch count! ːsteamhappyː[/p][p][/p][p][/p][h2]📝 The Changelog[/h2][p]Since this is the [b]first changelog for the public test branch here on Steam[/b], I have to start somewhere![/p][p][/p][p]If I tried to list [i]everything[/i] that’s changed compared to the current main branch version, it would be massive, so I’ll save that for the [b]Major Update[/b] post when it officially goes live on the main branch.[/p][p][/p][p]For now, I’m starting with just the [b]highlights[/b], picking up from where I left off in [b]Discord[/b] and the [b]Community Gazette[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]So, here’s the first official changelog for the [b]publictest[/b] branch on Steam![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/5538d04e795a15220cb873ab17c3f1a41a22a781.png"][/img][/p][h3]⚡ Switchboard[/h3][p]While most of the utility system upgrades are planned for the upcoming [b]Seasons Update[/b] and [b]Architecting Heights[/b], I’ve decided to release one of them early — because I know the late-game [b]electricity spaghetti[/b] was driving some players nuts. 😅[/p][p]Introducing the [b]Switchboard[/b]:[/p][list][*][p]Place a switchboard to [b]merge all electrical connections[/b] from items in a room.[/p][/*][*][p]You only need to connect the switchboard to the [b]main power line[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]It will auto-connect to everything else in that room, greatly reducing wire clutter.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][img notes.title: Community Gazette - Issue #6 - Garage, Vehicles, Agents and the City
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Back again with another Community Gazette! If you've been following development closely—especially on the public test branch—you probably already know that we’re reaching the final stage of the base game rebuild.

We’ve just wrapped up work on the final core system: public transportation, which builds on the transportation & rating revamp. It’s the last major content piece before we move into the polish and balance phase. With this, the main gameplay loop we've been designing is finally complete.

And that means we’re almost ready to ship something special to the main branch: a massive, unexpected update we’re calling "Echoes of the Community". It wasn’t even on the roadmap, but here it comes.


[h3]So, what’s changed since the last gazette?[/h3]
Originally, the goal for this update was pretty straightforward: take public transportation out of the research tree, let players buy buses, subways, and taxis, and set up schedules. Done and done.

But… if you know me a little by now, you’ll probably guess what happened next. I just couldn’t help myself, I had to add more details to the system, even though I knew we were already running behind schedule.. This update already started to feel like a second early access launch, so I wanted to rework this system to be more fun to manage, not just something you check off once and forget.

So it’s grown, maybe a little more than planned, but I think in a good way. Here’s what you’ll find in the new public transportation system:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/68c1de1b772ea4658e40e53272d84b49f2cd168d.jpg[/img]

[h3]Public Transit – Rebuilt from the Ground Up[/h3]
You’ll now need to buy, sell, and maintain your public transportation vehicles. That includes taxis, buses, subway trains, and wagons, each with their own stats and quirks. Just like walkways, you’ll need to get licenses from the city before you can run these services, but there’s a catch… which ties into a new dynamic with the townsfolk. More on that in a second.

Vehicles now have condition ratings—from Brand New to Like New, Fair, and Bad—and these affect everything: price, upkeep, even how often they break down. You’ll also deal with maintenance intervals, fuel costs, and yes, even vehicle mileage, which tracks how many round trips each vehicle makes between the casino and the city.

Higher mileage means lower resale value and more wear and tear—but also a cheaper price up front. Whether you invest in shiny new subway cars or pick up a few well-worn buses to get started is entirely up to you.

[h3]Maintenance & Mechanics[/h3]
Just like items and rooms in your casino, transportation vehicles need maintenance, but they do it in their own way. Each one has a maintenance interval (how many rounds it lasts) and a maintenance cost when it’s time to service it. These numbers depend on the vehicle’s base stats, its condition, and a little RNG from the dealer you bought it from.

If that sounds like a lot to micromanage, don’t worry. The idea is that, instead of constantly doing research, you'll be tinkering with different elements to expand your transportation capacity and automate tasks. Then, you'll revisit these aspects over time to keep improving. That's why you’ll now be able to contract mechanics as Agents to automate the process. Which brings us to…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/308952e5d5801e8ef257111eec1b1bcf110e3272.png[/img]

[h3]Introducing: The Agent System[/h3]
We’re adding a new type of professional to the game: Agents. These are freelancers you can contract temporarily for specific roles and tasks. Unlike your regular employees and contractor workers, they operate outside your business and come with different perks and limits.

For now, the Agent system includes:
[list]
[*] Drivers
[*] Train Operators
[*] Mechanics
[*] Lawyers (Will be moved to this)
[/list]
You’ll need drivers and operators to actually run your public transport vehicles. They also work as part of the scheduling system, hire one for mornings, and they’ll cover that shift hours automatically. Want full-day service? You’ll need two, but that also means faster mileage, more wear, and higher costs.

In future updates, more agent types will be introduced. Think detectives (for spying on rival casinos in the Rivalry update), or art dealers to track down rare pieces in the Luxury Amenities update.

[h3]A Bigger City, A Deeper Connection[/h3]
Your casino isn’t the only thing growing. Every bus, taxi, or subway line leads to the city, and the city’s going to matter more than ever.

To get licenses, you’ll need to build relationships with the townsfolk, especially if you want to run something like a subway line. The more you grow your public transportation network, the more important those connections become.

And this ties into the bigger picture: the city system will eventually connect to upcoming updates like Go Global, Rivalry, Catastrophes, and Advanced Logistics. This is just the start.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/f0346823df30999f2ef4e2041a55d63f5943ec0c.png[/img]

[h3]What's Next? The Polish Phase[/h3]
Once this update hits the Public Test Branch, we’ll begin the polishing and balancing process. After that, everything gets pushed to the main branch as a complete rebuild of the base game, and we shift into full-on content updates.

The polishing tasks are much smaller and quicker to complete. I’ve always been the kind of person who prefers to get the big heavy lifts out of the way early, and now it finally feels like the construction is done and we’re moving on to interior design. This is the fun part.

Here’s what’s coming in the final polish update:
[list]
[*] Redesigned townsfolk quests and decision UI
[*] Balancing of the main game loop values
[*] Final implementation of missing AI behaviors (e.g., animations for the hood hair dryer, cigar lounge ashtrays)
[*] Audio remastering
[*] New UX for negotiations
[*] Tutorial improvements
[*] Visual & audio effect polish
[*] Some key quality-of-life UI upgrades (with more in the QOL patch after Nightlife)
[/list]

[h3]Wrapping Up[/h3]
I truly believe this rebuilt version of the game feels like a second early access launch, and it’s going to give us a strong foundation for all the content that’s coming next. Once polish is complete, we’re heading full speed into expansions, features, and chaos.

Thanks for being part of this wild ride and helping shape this unique, deep, and sometimes delightfully chaotic simulation.

See you in the next Gazette, Cheers!

notes.title: Community Gazette - Issue #5 - Starting Map Size, Community Save File Sharing
notes.content:
Hey!👋

I hope your year has started off great! We’re finally about to launch the next update, kicking off a pipeline of content updates. I’m really excited about it. It’s time for another Community Gazette to go over what’s been happening since the end of the holiday season.

[h3]Starting Map Size System & The Go Global Update[/h3]
For a while now, we’ve had three map sizes to choose from when starting a game. However, many in our community have requested different ratios, larger maps, or even more basement floors than upper floors. To address this, I’ve added an even bigger map size and implemented a customizable map system where you can set the width/height ratio and the percentage of basement floors before starting. This feature is live on the public test branch and will roll out to the default branch with the Echoes of the Community update package. Sorry for the delay in getting this to you, public test players! I had to address some issues with the transportation system while implementing it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/8e9520f85471b0e340d8204f3b369bb9bbaa8287.jpg[/img]

But the most significant part? This ties into the upcoming Go Global update. In the future, you’ll manage multiple casinos in different cities, each with unique challenges. Map sizes and settings will play a crucial role in this system. This means the customization options may be revisited again before the 1.0 launch, but for now, these settings should provide a solid foundation.

[h3]Financial Data Graphs & Transaction Names[/h3]
I’ve finalized the casino data collection and financial graph system I mentioned earlier. The financial data graph is now live on the public test branch, with additional graphs coming in the next patch after some UI tweaks.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/e66de6bcd182d8ebf2ac015fbec288d76f73b884.gif[/img]

If you’ve been using an older public test save, you might notice some outdated transaction names or financial data for casino rooms at first. However, as new data comes in, everything should gradually align with the latest system.

[h3]Transportation System Refactor & Vehicle Changes[/h3]
There was one part of the transportation module that hadn't been refactored during the past backend work campaign. It stood firm, a stable, a shrine of old code, if you will. 😊 However, since unlocking worker trucks and private cars, bugs have been creeping in. So, I decided to give the system a proper overhaul and migrate it to the new vehicle garage system too.
So Heads-up: After updating, you might notice all your cars have disappeared when loading an old public test save for the first time. Your people might also complain about not finding their cars, but in theory, everything should settle smoothly after that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/729c89bad4273504ffd68360d2de3130fdab5d36.jpg[/img]

[h3]Cheat Panel & Final Pre-Balance Features[/h3]
The public test branch is still out of balance so the "Cheat Panel" is still active for you to use while testing, but I have two key features left to improve before tackling the game’s balance update. Yes, improvements can go on forever, but I know, you know, we all know that these two features are essential before we can truly feel satisfied and move on to the content phase of the roadmap 😅
[olist]
[*] Building Research Overhaul – I plan to move the building research tree to a licensing system, similar to transportation. This means using administrative documents and money to purchase building licenses, improving permits and elevator specifications.
[*] Hiring Negotiations – While we introduced auto-hiring through the HR Manager, the negotiation messaging system still feels a bit clunky. I want to improve both its UX and mechanics as part of the Echoes of the Community update.
[/olist]

[h3]Next Steps & Community Save File Sharing[/h3]
The plan (which can't stop changing) is as follows:
[list]
[*] Later today or tomorrow – A hotfix patch addressing collected reports (huge thanks to everyone who submitted them!).
[*] Next focus – Completing the transportation system, then implementing negotiation improvements and building licensing.
[*] Final stage – Game balance, quality of life and polish update, which will be released as a major default branch update.
[/list]

Since balance is on the horizon, I’ve created a new Discord channel called “Save It and Leave It.” Here’s the cinematic channel description:
Submit Your Legendary Saves! Got an epic, oversized, or glorious save file? Share it here! I’ll use it to test and balance the game, and the community can explore and enjoy it too. Whether it’s for inspiration, chaos, or just curiosity, your save could make an impact!
So, feel free to drop your saves into the channel, especially when you’ve wrapped up a casino and are moving on to a new one. This will help me tremendously in balancing the game, and it’ll also serve as a space where you and other players can share and review save files. Eventually, I’ll implement Steam Workshop support for an even smoother experience.

Thanks for Being Part of the Community!
That’s all for this week’s update! I appreciate all of you for being part of this journey. 

See you in the next one!
Cheers!
