notes.title: Community Gazette - Issue #3 - What’s Brewing for the Public Test?
notes.content:
Hello! 😊
I think I’m starting to get the hang of this development journaling thing, who would’ve thought? 

First and foremost, I wanted to share that the changes and updates that I mentioned in the last weekly gazette have been uploaded to the public test server after some internal testing with my partner hopefully wihout breaking too much. This patch unlocks the entire new hotel and laundry system along with the hotel menu. If you’re someone who enjoys participating in public testing and maybe reporting issues, this is your chance to dive in and explore.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/7a834084a633893641cc54b63b50ed66f35e1bb9.png[/img]

With that said, let’s jump into what we’ve been working on behind the scenes this week.

[h3]The Revamped Vehicle Parking System & UI[/h3]
As mentioned in the last post, where we explored changes to the walkways and transportation systems, this week’s focus has been on completing the remaining transportation mechanics in the public test build, starting with vehicle parking!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/1583ec20965af1dedbfea066003b67e74a250086.png[/img]

To streamline things, all transport systems have been removed from the research tree. This means parking spaces now start unlocked, allowing you to jump right in. However, as your parking needs grow, you’ll still require accounting and HR documents to secure government licenses for expanding your parking capacity.

Another addition is the ability to build parking spots for contractors like builders, delivery drivers, garbage collectors, or police officers. This gives you greater control over how your spaces are utilized and helps optimize the flow of people and services.

I’ve also worked on a new parking menu that doubles as a handy data minimap and a place to buy government licenses. It shows who’s arriving and leaving, the number of licensed spaces you have, how many are in use, and other useful insights.

[h3]The Revamped Public Transportation System & UI[/h3]
Public transportation; taxis, buses, and subways has also received a major overhaul. Like parking spaces and walkways, these systems now start unlocked. However, you’ll need to construct and upgrade a garage to operate these services.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/32144e71fa1d368e578f1c9a8feff117250727c2.png[/img]

From there, you can purchase vehicles like taxis, shuttles, buses, or subway trains, and schedule their operation. You can run your vehicles 24/7 by contracting drivers to both morning and night shifts, but it will lead to faster wear and tear. Upgrading your garage will also unlock automated vehicle maintenance, helping you keep the operation running smoothly.

Thanks to the revamped transportation systems’ integration with the new service capacity and rating system, you should now have a clearer view of each transportation need to make decisions. This allows you to adapt your operations to meet growing demands efficiently.

[h3]Vending System Changes and Additions[/h3]
In the previous version of the game, vending machines functioned more as room decorations, with customers using them as part of their room interaction modules. Back then, vending options included tobacco machines, cold drink machines, hot drink machines, and snack machines. During Early Access, we expanded the interactivity of bookshelves and newspaper racks, allowing customers to use them as vending-like items that generated income for the player, though these didn’t require inventory items.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/a340f522471ea00b2eb36e9844f252a8f0edf47e.png[/img]

With this update, I’ve written a new behavior script dedicated to vending machine usage, making these interactions more accessible throughout the casino hotel.

Bookshelves and newspaper racks now require inventory items to operate. There are four newspaper varieties and six book varieties available for you to stock, enabling customers to choose their favorites. Additionally, candy machines and keychain machines have been reclassified as vending machines. Candy machines now need candy bars as inventory items, while keychain machines require keychains.
We’ve also added two new vending items, pipe vending stands and lighter vending stands, to complement the new cigar shop feature. These vending machines come with corresponding inventory requirements.

[h3]Large Dumpsters and Cigarette Bins[/h3]
Based on valuable feedback from our Discord community, we’ve added large dumpsters and cigarette bins to improve waste management.

Customers who smoke will now look for a cigarette bin after finishing their cigarette. Failing to provide enough bins in smoking-friendly areas will result in more trash accumulation and, with the upcoming Catastrophes update, it could even pose a fire hazard.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/79660a67fe55b7ac329caef80ca7e4d51e65b499.png[/img]

On the dumpster side, we’ve introduced a larger dumpster that takes up slightly less space than two standard dumpsters but can hold more waste than both combined.

[h3]Room Signs[/h3]
Previously, closed rooms displayed signs during restricted service hours. We’ve expanded this feature to include a variety of visual indicators.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/2923281cbf271dfd984b479e06de4aa5aec905dd.png[/img]

Thanks to new sign drawings from Nil, rooms now display small signs that you can hover over for important updates. These signs highlight issues like essential item shortage, pathfinding problems, construction status, and low room ratings depending on the room type.
This update adds a clearer, more intuitive layer of management to your casino hotel, ensuring you can address the issues you choose quickly and efficiently.

[h3]Personal Stuff[/h3]
As some of you may already know, we’re a two-person game studio, just my partner and me. Alongside the development work mentioned earlier, this past week has been a bit chaotic as we’ve been in the middle of an international move we’ve been planning for a while.
This is also why this week’s Weekly Gazette is a couple of days late, I just couldn’t find the time to get it out on schedule. Normally, I aim to post updates every week between Saturday and Monday, and I believe we’re back on track to maintain that schedule moving forward.

[h3]What Are the Current Plans?[/h3]
Here’s what’s on the near horizon: First, I’ll be uploading the remaining transportation changes discussed here to the public test server. After that, I plan to dedicate a week to animation and ai behaviour polishing, balancing, bug fixing, and working on tutorials, UI improvements, and data graphs. This will also include merging save files from the default branch with those from the public test branch. Once all that’s done, the Echoes of the Community update will be ready to launch on the default branch.
Looking ahead, I’m aiming to complete testing for the Nightlife update before the New Year. Most of it is already finished, I prefering to not to make promises. I’m trying to avoid unnecessary extra stress if unexpected issues pop up this time. 😊

That about sums it up for this week! Thank you all for your continued support and patience during the development of Casino Resort Tower, it means the world to us. I’ll see you in the next one.
Cheers!

notes.title: Community Gazette - Issue #2 - New Laundry and Hotel System, New Hotel Menu
notes.content:
Hi everyone! 😊

This week, we’ve been busy improving the hotel system AIs and crafting a brand-new hotel menu. Along the way, I also tackled several fixes and balance adjustments. These updates should be live on the public test branch in just a couple of days. After that, I’ll focus on the final touches for the transportation system. Once that’s complete, we’ll be ready to merge everything into the default branch for the release of the "Echoes of the Community" update and kick off public testing for the "Nightlife" update.

Here’s a closer look at what’s been in the works this week:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/b68f8cdcf01b27caad7c648ca42a9405f222dc4a.png[/img]

[h3]Laundry System Overhaul[/h3]
Dirty sheets will now function as physical objects within the game, similar to trash in the waste management system. You’ll need to store these "by-products" of guest services and remove them efficiently. Housekeepers can collect and deposit dirty sheets into laundry bins, which can then be processed in washing machines and iron presses.
The new system encourages players to identify and address bottlenecks by managing housekeeper numbers, storage capacity for dirty linens, and available washing machines and presses. And the new hotel menu, along with detailed data graphs, will provide all the insights you need to stay on top of things!

[h3]Hotel System AI and Behavior Updates[/h3]
Housekeepers:
I’ve completely rewritten the housekeeper AI for improved performance and streamlined behavior. Housekeepers now operate in two key work states instead of one randomized one:
Collecting dirty sheets – They can pick up to three sheets at a time and deposit them into the nearest available laundry bin.
Cleaning and ironing – They retrieve dirty sheets from bins in their assigned laundry rooms, wash them, and iron clean sheets for reuse.
Housekeepers prioritize laundry bins based on their assignment, be it a assigned room, a patrol route base room, or the closest available bin if unassigned.
Guests:
Guests can now use luxury amenities, such as hot tubs, in high-end rooms. We’ve added new behaviors and mood modifiers for these items, making the guest experience more dynamic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/1f6b1d080a8e828309e94f0becd93e2d0caad891.png[/img]
[h3]The Hotel Menu[/h3]
The newly designed hotel menu provides an at-a-glance overview of room occupancy rates, laundry bin capacity, counts and capacities of key housekeeping items. You’ll also have the option to open or close rooms for bookings, whether to catch up on services or manage other hotel operations.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/e221fd806fb1b0585e52a6af4223a7bfc573b4a6.png[/img]
[h3]Customer Inventory[/h3]
Borrowing from the employee inventory system, customers are now have an inventory too. This feature allows players to see what guests are carrying, such as casino chips, souvenirs, or vending machine purchases.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/6cc128f3bec8cfa029d3398d79192b1f4ae44a13.png[/img]
Finally, we’ve decided to add a special touch to the main menu: a little character to honor the memory of Bacon, our beloved pug, and a cherished member of our development team. We hope this small tribute keeps his playful spirit alive in our hearts and the game.


Until next time,
Tolgahan

notes.title: Community Gazette - Issue #1 - What Is Community Gazette?, A Recap
notes.content:
[h3]What is the Community Gazette?[/h3]
Originally, I intended to use Steam’s news feed only for major updates, when things were polished and closer to a commercially playable state. For those who wanted to be more involved in the development journey, we had our Discord as a place to dive into the "behind-the-scenes" work, gather feedback, and have discussions with the community. I’m also always available in the Steam community hub to answer questions and consider suggestions.

This approach seemed like a good balance, keeping Steam's news feed focused on major, ready-to-play updates for those who preferred final highlights without frequent updates on the ongoing development process. However, after an objection from a community member, I realized there are many of you who are interested in the development progress but may not wish to use platforms like Discord.

With that in mind, I’ve decided to start a regular news post: Community Gazette. Each weekend, I'll share a snapshot of what's happening behind the scenes, discuss future plans, and provide a closer look at our journey toward release. This way, those who prefer not to join Discord can still stay in the loop.

Alongside these posts, I’ll continue to post separate update/change logs whenever there are significant updates to the main game.


[h3]How is the Public Test Branch Going? A Recap[/h3]
Since this is the first issue of Weekly Community Gazette, let’s do a quick recap!

For those following along on Discord or in the community hub, you might know we kicked off a significant refactoring and rewriting phase a few months back. Given the scope of the project and our ambitious roadmap, there are some exciting content-focused updates in the pipeline. To support large-scale simulations running smoothly over time, we chose to invest this time in overhauling the core systems.

After completing the refactoring phase, I’ve implemented nearly all the features and changes we discussed together on the community hub and Discord. I’ll be posting a comprehensive changelog with the upcoming default branch update, but you can already check them by switching to the public test branch right now. Here’s a quick look at some of the most-requested features that have been implemented following the backend work:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/272da870b91cb7f406e4cdd3fc495811c0e980bc.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Rating System Refactoring:[/b] I've overhauled the hotel rating system, changing how ratings are sampled and adjusting level thresholds. Basically, daily ratings will now vary between -100/+100, making it clearer for you to make informed decisions about your casino hotel and giving me clearer numbers to work with while balancing the game.
[*] [b]End-Day Report:[/b] There's now a single end-day report that includes multiple reports about transportation capacity, service capacity, daily guest traffic report, links to the data info graphics, guest appeal, rating, and some administrative windows like tax and salary payment.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/5f78620c10a40e290b52ca6529bca5ebf60c965b.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]New Transportation System:[/b] I’ve removed all transportation-related stuff from the research tree. Going forward, to meet your casino hotel’s transportation capacity needs, you’ll focus on regularly upgrading/constructing walkways and managing your garage. This includes buying, selling, and repairing public transport vehicles as needed, rather than simply scheduling them. Additionally, instead of unlocking features through research, you’ll now acquire licenses to build bus stops, parking lots, taxi ranks, etc.
[*] [b]Daily Attracted Customers:[/b] The new mechanics now include a finite number of daily customers, based on both service capacity and hotel rating, rather than just an instant number of attracted customers, with the help of new walkways and transportation stuff. This makes each customer more valuable to manage and send off happy.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/9ba9016a46b4de886261484e14615996f9b2a149.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Item Usage Queue:[/b] In the old system, folks would wander around items they wanted to use, and whoever checked back first got to use it when it was free. Now, items have a queue capacity. People will form clear lines to use them if they're queueable. They'll enter the line, start a timer, and if they wait too long, they'll get angry and leave the casino hotel. You can see how many people are in line, the order of people, how long they've waited, and if they're happy by hovering over the queue or using the item's info menu. If the usage position of the item is on the left side, they'll start the line on the right side and vice versa. The line will always stay in the room and curve to the other side if necessary. This system also talks with the new room capacity and renewed hotel rating system.
[*] [b]Asynchronous AI Item and Room Searching:[/b] Every time an entity with decision-making abilities takes action, it usually searches for a specific item or room from a huge list of objects. As you can imagine, this happens a lot in CRT and can cause frame drops if too many searches occur at once. To tackle this, I've created a new search engine-like system that's asynchronous and CPU multi-threaded. It collects all search requests, prioritizes them, checks the CPU load, and decides how many to execute per frame, making others wait for the next frame. This spreads the workload over time, boosting FPS, especially for massive casinos with thousands of entities.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/0f8a52bb93dd035c7a62b65109e6b9026e8509ab.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Escalators:[/b] Escalators have been added as a more guest-friendly alternative to stairs, especially in places where you don't want to place elevators. Customers will now leave if they have to climb more than 5 stairs to reach their destination, but this limit is extended to 15 for escalators. If an escalator isn’t powered, guests will treat it as regular stairs. Additionally, I’ve increased the movement speed penalty for stairs. The image shows the current state from the public test, but we've decided to make escalators 2 tiles long instead of one. More varieties, like stairs, will also be added.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/2c4bb1d483201191135bded81ad0503954f0c412.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Executives System:[/b] You can now hire executives such as an HR Manager, Finance Manager, Research Manager, and Marketing Manager. Each of these roles has an attention value of 100, which can be assigned to different tasks to automate processes like hiring/firing employees, auto-paying taxes and salaries, or boosting various parts of your business.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/af7c0ce1cf2846ec8622faf6da79d880ffc8c32d.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Room Capacity System:[/b] I've added a room capacity value to the public service rooms. It's calculated by room size and available items related to the room type. Now customers don't enter full capacity rooms even for waiting for a service. Room capacity value also determines the overall service capacity of your casino hotel. Factors like transportation capacity and hotel rating influence how much of this capacity is utilized.
[*] [b]Separate Room Policies:[/b] You can now set the work hours and pricing of the rooms separately using the policy menu or the room's own information menu even if they have the same room type.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/7608bee0995bad83465be26ca17cf297d75d75f5.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Data Recording and Info Graphs:[/b] I’ve added a system that tracks almost every bit of transactional or situational data in your casino hotel. This includes Financial Data, Rating Data, Office and Archive Data, Happiness Data, Security and Crime Data, Utility Data, Transportation Data, Inventory and Storage Data, Environment Data, Cuisine Services Data, Entertainment Services Data, Hospitality Services Data, and Leisure Services Data. You'll be able to visualize these datas with new infographics and charts, as well as interact with them throughout the UI such as item-based menus.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/5f4f8a2988c26bb34b8bced1e10be0f106767733.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Contractors System:[/b] You can now select the number of outsourced workers such as builders, waste collectors, and delivery persons you want to hire using the contractor's menu. However, these workers also have an hourly rate calculated based on the number of people you call.
[*] [b]Specialized Parking Spaces:[/b] You can now place designated parking spaces for police, builders, delivery persons, and waste collectors to increase efficiency.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d96fe706aff787da7a757bdbcce51240a7dfc492.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]People Inventory System:[/b] You will now be able to clearly see what people are carrying on them from their menu, such as trash bags for janitors, menu items for customers, tools for maintenance officers, and so on.
[*] [b]Employee Quitting:[/b] Employees experiencing extended periods of unhappiness are now more likely to quit. You can check their quit probability directly in their UI window.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/0b824bef3f517e118e1174f9af8aa93e70b0d79b.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]Employee Break Room Item Need:[/b] Employees now look for their favorite break room item and throw a tantrum if it's not available. They end up spending more time in a tantrum than they would if the item were available.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/8ed41ac9964e7f539aa87a2e55fce5a908d98532.jpg[/img]

[list]
[*] [b]UI Improvements:[/b] Many UI improvements have been made, both in terms of design and performance. This includes a service-type-based reports menu, adding every room type to smoking policies menu, changes to item types in the item selection menu, a rehaul of the research menu, and many other updates. I’ll share more details once the update is released to the default branch.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/120b251382a418306e7f16079fda433ac5d37211.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/18be1422b7df908add1e944efebfa63df5035ac3.jpg[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/326baf60021586dfe4bbd74ffce86350b752b04e.jpg[/img]

We’ve also added some content-based features that aren’t directly related to the upcoming Nightlife Update but were requested frequently. These include specialized cuisine services like an Asian Fusion Restaurant, Italian Ristorante, Mexican Cantina, Seafood Restaurant, French Bistro, Smoothie Bar, and Steakhouse. Additionally, we’ve added leisure and amenities options such as a Cigar Lounge, Cyber Cafe, Hair Salon, and Yoga Studio.

As I mentioned, you can get a sneak peak to all of these changes by switching to the public test branch. Feel free to share your feedback on the Community Hub, Discord, or Reddit if you do!

[h3]So, What’s Coming Next?[/h3]
After working through and testing all these updates with the help of the community, we were about to start testing some of the remaining core features for the "Nightlife" update, such as the new calendar and events system, nightclubs, and more. However, there's been a shift in our plans. With so many tweaks to the core mechanics, the current public test version of the game has evolved quite a bit compared to the older version on the default branch. To make this transition smoother, I’ve decided to split the update into two parts.

The first part, titled “Echoes of the Community” (since it covers most of the feedback and suggestions from Discord and the community hub), will be a mid-major update released just before the “Nightlife” update. This update will include what’s currently on the test branch, along with the final adjustments to the transportation and hotel systems, and some last requested features from the feedback channel. I’ll also focus on completing data graphs, polishing AI behaviors, balancing, and audio improvements to prepare for the release. As part of this, I’ve temporarily removed the remaining unreleased content from the front-end (though it’s still functioning in the background) and will hold that back for a later release to the default branch. This way, we can polish the features we have now and deliver them to the default branch much sooner, like very soon!

I think that covers everything for this first Weekly Community Gazette. Thanks again for all your support! I really appreciate your patience and your feedback, it’s been invaluable in shaping the game. As always, feel free to reach out on the Community Hub, Discord, or Reddit if you have any questions or thoughts.

I'll see you in the next one!

[list]

notes.title: [GAME UPDATE] v0.7FH Update Is Here!
notes.content:
Hey everyone! Another update! ːsteamhappyː


[h2]UPDATE HIGHLIGHTS[/h2]


[h3]Lawsuits System[/h3]
Customers can now initiate lawsuits against you, seeking compensation for various grievances like witnessing a crime or enduring subpar room conditions. These could range from cleanliness concerns to decoration and lighting issues.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/e5f1331ea8bc3c75347446d7df4e70af49ad82c8.png[/img]
When faced with a lawsuit, you can opt to wait for the court date. The outcome hinges on the winning chance of the case – a successful defense incurs no payment and zero additional managerial documents. However, a loss demands full compensation along with associated managerial document costs.

You also have the option to settle with the plaintiff before the court date. If you choose to settle you will only need to pay the agreed amount and use some documents.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/3e74a925656c4e060f4c4d925400568dce95412f.png[/img]
And the legal representation! Lawyers can be hired for cases, each equipped with negotiation and courthouse skills. Negotiation skills reduce settlement costs, while courthouse skills boost the chances of a favorable court outcome. The cost of hiring a lawyer is influenced by both the player's available funds and the lawyer's skill points.


[h3]Transportation/People Spawn System Refactoring[/h3]
So, there were some issues with our transportation and spawn system – you know, people complaining about missing buses or employees showing up on their days off. Anyway, I decided to dive into the code, one thing led to another and I ended up writing the whole thing from scratch:D. Along the way, I made some small changes to the way things look on the surface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d73480115ddbbcc1aab56f402d7667a2a3e93b9d.png[/img]
In the old system, when someone wanted to spawn, we'd check their favorite transportation type and see if there was a spot available in two hours. But that caused problems – employees showing up late, customers missing buses – not good.

Now, if a customer wants to hit the casino hotel, the system checks for availability in a 3-hour window for both arrivals and departures. No more gaps in customer transportation. And for employees who love the bus, we prioritize slots at 5 pm and 5 am – they come on foot if there's no space or scheduled bus, and we give them a negative moodlet.

Subway's got a similar deal at 4 pm and 4 am, parking lots and taxis are buzzing between 5-7 pm and 5-7 am. I've also added little icons to the transportation menu about it.

So, with these changes, buses, trains, and taxis should be packed with people according to their favorite transportation type when you cover all the scheduled times.



[h3]FIXES:[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/3762b22aa286e63a65901d7b6ca64b20157aab37.png[/img]
[h3]Prestige System for Rooms[/h3]
The room tier system has undergone a transformation, introducing the new room prestige system. Each room type now encompasses five distinct prestige levels, each with its own set of buffs and requirements for advancing to the next level.

To elevate a room's prestige level, you must fulfill its specific needs in terms of room values or required items. Additionally, rooms with higher prestige levels contribute rating points during each shift, in addition to the buffs associated with their room type. This marks a significant shift in the way rooms are graded and rewarded.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/ca49e970e9198cddcb7fbe9f42f792401b33839a.png[/img]
[h3]High Roller Room[/h3]
Introducing an exclusive experience for our esteemed patrons. A new type of casino room for wealthy customers. You can set the betting prices of this room separately from the pricing menu and its base prices are higher than the regular casino room. It has slightly different needs for each prestige level and customers with a 'Poor' and 'Middle-Class' wealth type don't use this room.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/a976b8177b464f945b45125aee76e56817b4433d.png[/img]

We've made some additions and changes to the jackpot system Now, when a player strikes gold with a jackpot, the entire room erupts in joy, converging near the winner. You will now also receive rating points for the amount won in the jackpot which will be communicated with a pop-up window. The chances of someone hitting the jackpot have been given a significant boost, and this probability keeps growing as the jackpot pool expands. [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/1f2cc3656943e4727a4e0f82aaa288ff3509a9db.png[/img]

Hey there, everyone!

We've been a little quiet lately, but I promise it's for a good reason. ːsteamhappyː We've been working hard behind the scenes, doing some major refactoring and creating some cool tools to speed up the release of our upcoming major updates. [h2]UPDATE HIGHLIGHTS[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/625b568265650e88c7f4d00a9767fbdcc706f953.png[/img]
[h3]CCTV Enhancements[/h3]
We've introduced some important improvements to the CCTV system. Now, the CCTV cameras and monitoring tables are interconnected through receivers and transmitters. When cameras are placed, they will automatically connect to nearby transmitters, and monitoring stations will link to the placed receivers if they are within range. The complete CCTV network is established by connecting a transmitter to a receiver. Receivers can be linked to multiple transmitters, and each connected monitoring station increases the capacity of the CCTV network by 6.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/65953528b20ae74dfb9c2fc1fc3457d9ce8922f5.png[/img]
[h3]Sports Lounge and Betting[/h3]
We've added a fresh entertainment type for your guests with the introduction of our sports lounge. Now, you can build a dedicated sports lounge area, install sports betting kiosks, and designate various sports betting options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/f68d194679c2b94e3550ee7237b105a4d1a03d4c.png[/img]
[h3]Employee Assignments and Patrol Routes[/h3]
Employees such as maintenance officers, janitors, housekeepers, security officers, and vendors can also be assigned to patrol routes that you have created other than rooms. Additionally, our HR menu has undergone a complete revamp for more straightforward assignment management.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/bc45ef0869cf69f2bcb653c66f92dfffe05cc35e.png[/img]
[h3]Employee Job Satisfaction[/h3]
Employee happiness is no longer solely determined by moodlets. Now, employees' job satisfaction is influenced by the amenities in the employee break room. Each employee has their preferred break room items, snacks, and drinks. If their job satisfaction remains consistently low, they may decide to leave their position.

[h3]Customer Satisfaction[/h3]
Customers arrive at our casino hotel with specific expectations, typically involving 4-6 primary services they wish to enjoy. Customer satisfaction is now based on whether we can meet these expectations or not, considering any unforeseen service unavailability.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/202f696c9102ae59066589b455450b2364bd2e97.png[/img]
[h3]Employee Break Scheduling[/h3]
We've introduced more flexibility into our employees' break schedules. Each of the two shifts now offers three different break times. You have the freedom to customize these break times to ensure a seamless service flow and prevent any disruptions.

notes.title: About CRT #14 | Security
notes.content:
Casino Resort Tower (CRT) will be available for early access tomorrow! I can hardly believe it's finally happening.

CRT is a detailed simulation, with a wide range of mechanics to explore. Unfortunately, I couldn't cover all of these mechanics that will be available with the EA release in my previous 'About CRT' posts during the playtesting and heavy development phase. Moreover, those older posts have become somewhat irrelevant now, as we have added a lot more content and made significant improvements.

To address this, I have come up with a plan (Yeay). I will go back and rewrite the old posts to bring them up-to-date, ensuring they reflect the current state of the game. Additionally, I will be posting about the remaining topics in between updates and patches, leading up to the first major content update after the early access release.

Anyways, let's talk about today's topics: security, crime, customer detention, CCTV systems, and officer deployments.


[h3]ROOM SECURITY[/h3]
Each room within the casino hotel possesses a security value, which can be influenced by various factors. The presence of certain items may decrease the room's security value, thereby increasing the likelihood of crimes occurring. To enhance the security value of a room, CCTV cameras can be installed or security officers can be deployed in public areas. In private spaces like hotel rooms, security can be bolstered by installing burglar alarms and safe boxes. These measures contribute to maintaining a higher level of security, ensuring the safety and well-being of both customers and hotel staff.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/c0a23e77b50fefd92ce73cc4067dce9d896bd03a.gif[/img]

[h3]CRIME[/h3]
In the diverse environment of the casino hotel, various types of crimes can occur in different types of rooms. For instance, rooms with reception and shop counters are vulnerable to crimes like credit card fraud. On the other hand, casinos are susceptible to crimes such as card switching and dice sliding. Each crime committed within the premises results in a deduction of a rating point from the casino hotel. However, the rating point can be recovered by effectively detaining suspects involved in criminal activities. To minimize the likelihood of crimes occurring, it is crucial to enhance the security values of the respective rooms.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/0c976bc840b946e1db6689efea46194d3eeaa525.gif[/img]

[h3]SECURITY OFFICER DEPLOYMENT[/h3]
Once you've hired security officers, you can enhance security in public rooms by deploying them. The presence of a patrolling security officer significantly boosts room security. To make a room deployable, access the security menu by clicking on the security button located at the bottom right of the screen. Then, select the security officer deployment button and choose the desired room on the map to make it deployable. Security officers will automatically occupy the selected rooms unless they are engaged in detaining unruly customers.

[h3]CCTV SYSTEMS[/h3]
CCTV cameras provide a convenient solution for boosting room security without the requirement of deploying security officers. Once a CCTV camera is installed in a room, it must be connected to a CCTV monitoring table for functionality. These monitoring tables can only be placed in security offices, and each table can accommodate up to four CCTV cameras. To initiate the process of connecting CCTV cameras with CCTV monitoring tables, access the security menu by clicking on the security button located at the bottom right of the screen. Then, simply select the CCTV wiring button.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/1c1467bc2f4c251201d843c15a762995607d83c0.gif[/img]

[h3]CUSTOMER DETENTION[/h3]
When a customer engages in criminal behavior, it results in a deduction of a rating point. However, this lost rating point can be recovered by detaining the suspect. The detention process can commence following the occurrence of the illegal activity, provided there is a security officer available during the current shift and an available detention room. The security officer escorts the suspect to the designated detention room, places them in a holding cell, initiates the processing procedure, and contacts the police. A police officer is then dispatched to collect and transport the suspect.

notes.title: About CRT #13 | Casino
notes.content:
Hello hello! It's been a while since the last About CRT blog post. Today's post is about the casinos.

You know all of the bars, saunas, events, and so on are all good fun but every casino hotel makes a big buck from their casinos. So it's good to have a nice casino hotel with a variety of games for your guests. Because every customer has a favorite casino game,  and your casino hotel star rating is affected positively if they can find it.



[h3]CASINO CASHIER[/h3]
Some casino guests come to the casinos to watch the games and have some drinks. But if they want to gamble, they go to the casino cashiers to exchange some chips first. Don't forget to check if there are enough casino cashiers so they don't leave after waiting for too long.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/f61bef5fac9e9dafe625f1757926731bebc75ba6.gif[/img]

[h3]DICE GAMES[/h3]
Place dice games tables and assign a variety of dice games if you want please gamblers who want to roll the dice and take some chances.

[h3]FORTUNE WHEEL GAMES[/h3]
The only thing better than a game of chance is a game where there is a giant spinning wheel. So consider placing some fortune wheel desks too.

[h3]ROULETTE GAMES[/h3]
Place roulette tables so you can make money while your customers watch in horror as the roulette ball lands on the one number they didn't bet on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/84e775e4e370deb0e5e3f7b11ceb62131ee3c016.gif[/img]

[h3]SLOT GAMES[/h3]
Your guests can lose all of their money in seconds and still walk away feeling like a winner because the lights and sounds were really cool if you place slot machines and assign different kinds of slot games to them.

[h3]CARD GAMES[/h3]
Some gamblers want to show their patience, strategy, and ability. Place card games tables and assign card games such as blackjack, baccarat, and texas holdem poker to them.

[h3]BINGO GAMES[/h3]
If you want some customers that are yelling "BINGO!" here and there, you can place bingo desks and assign different bingo games to them.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/9a5652a3e127d549807c2618ba878db7d20c5df2.gif[/img]

[h3]KENO GAMES[/h3]
Make playing the lottery fun for your guest by placing keno machines and assigning games such as caveman keno, superball keno, and klub keno to them.

[h3]VIDEO POKER GAMES[/h3]
Sometimes gamblers want to feel like a high-roller without having to sit at a table with other people. Don't forget to place some video poker machines around too.


So yeah, managing a casino hotel may be a high-stakes game, but with the right strategy and attention to detail, you'll be able to create a thriving empire that keeps your guests coming back for more.

Have an awesome day, and I'll see you on the next post!

notes.title: About CRT #12 | Food & Drink Services
notes.content:
Hello everyone, welcome to another "About CRT" post. Hope everyone is doing great!

Let's talk about different ways you can serve some food and drinks to your guests at your casino hotel.


[h3]Restaurants[/h3]
Restaurants are a nice fine dining service that you can provide to your guests while getting high-profit margins. Well-off and middle-class customers are more likely to choose restaurants over vending machines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d03ddab58df2865d6660762526667ce83373166b.gif[/img]

[h3]Bars[/h3]
People love to have a few drinks especially in the evening and at the weekends. You can build bars and even organize bar events for your customers.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/0bd14b8a4e8d2b01379ed18d554153628e440381.gif[/img]

[h3]Cafes[/h3]
It's a good idea to extend your business by building a place for people who want to have some coffee in the morning. Cafes are also nice places to sell some desserts to your guests too.

[h3]Vending Machines[/h3]
Vending machines are the most basic food and drink service you can give to your customers and also to employees on the break. You can start selling snacks and drinks just by placing vending machines around your casino hotel and filling up your storage with goods.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/9c5df1f9115f0cd960b723283f1fcc2f32c4ce8d.png[/img]

[h3]Vendors[/h3]
You can hire vendors and assign them to patrol routes or rooms. They walk around with the menu items you have assigned and cause your customers to make some impulsive overpriced snack and drink purchases on the spot.

[h3]Mini Bars[/h3]
Mini bars are like vending machines you can put into hotel rooms. You can store some snacks and drinks in your inventory, and add them to the mini bar menu for the guest that loves to have some mini crackers or drinks before going to bed.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/eb7af642a7f862d3e147ff12f3e936a6937d3c83.png[/img]

[h3]Menus Management[/h3]
Every cuisine service has its own menu that you can manage. You can make your menus more classy and increase your hotel rating by researching menu items with high rating points and adding them to your relevant menus. Every menu item needs one or more inventory items to be created by your employees so keep an eye on your inventory while expanding your food and drinks services. You can check the "About CRT 3:  Inventory" if you want to learn more.


Yeap, I think this sums it up for the most part.

Let me know in the comments or from the discord server if you want to hear something more specific.
Have an awesome day and cheers!

notes.title: About CRT #11 | Transportation
notes.content:
Hello! We have been silently working on early access playtest for a while but I think it's time for another About CRT post. 


Oh, also I thank you for your interest in Casino Resort Tower during the Steam Fest! It was awesome!



Let's talk about today's About CRT topic: Transportation! 

Every customer has a favorite means of transportation in CRT. Their preferences are also affected by their wealth. Customers are more likely to prefer the bus, subway, or walking if they are poor. And they are more likely to prefer their cars or taxis if they are well-off. Having all of the options for the customers increases the casino hotel's rating so it means more customers and more money.



[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/4ceb6b2403174f5f429eed5297d8e35015257f3e.gif[/img]

[h3]Bus Stops[/h3]
You can rent and schedule different types of buses according to demand. There are three different types of buses. A shuttle bus is the smallest bus you can rent for start or for hours with low demand, a single deck bus is the mid-size standard bus, and the articulated bus is the biggest bus you can rent for rush hours.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/ee1d0f57496398f62f4818e08a693fdb337151a0.gif[/img]

[h3]Subway Stations[/h3]
You can rent two, three, or four wagon subway trains and schedule them to come up every other hour. You should manage it carefully so you don't lose money by renting unnecessary trains. If there is enough demand you should earn some profit.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/a0b037efe84ba9d5fcd7b30a73f5ffacbe186580.png[/img]

[h3]Parking Lots[/h3]
You can build parking lots underground and place parking spaces for the people who want to come to the casino hotel in their car. Some of the customers just leave without spending any money if all of your parking spaces are full so it's nice to keep an eye on that. You can also earn some extra money from parking if you didn't order parking service to be free from the Policies menu.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/72e19b00f1580f3f3a9650a592f1a7922c4a69a5.png[/img]

[h3]Taxi Ranks[/h3]
After you build a taxi rank, you can rent up to four taxis for each shift. Taxis wait at the rank during the time you rent for a customer to pick up from the hotel or another address.

notes.title: About CRT #10 | Policies
notes.content:
You can decide on different policies for your casino from the policies menu.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/ced89b47f5206d40b7669359eadec58730e3f33a.gif[/img]

[h2]Smoking Policies[/h2]
Some of the customers and employees are smokers. You can decide where people can smoke with smoking policies for the customers and employees separately. If you let everyone smoke anywhere it will make non-smokers unhappy. If you ban smoking completely it will make smokers unhappy. Smoking rooms come in handy if you have researched and placed them around.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/66ee98ef83148d711d01e2e9808b74964f5b9d38.png[/img]

[h2]Service Hours[/h2]
You can choose the service hours for the services you provide at your casino hotel. Each service can be open on the morning shift, night shift, or 24 hours if it's not closed. You should also make sure that there are enough employees on the related shifts.
Current service hours policies:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/fe3d7aaf0b150f05b0670abe22ded30969037e5b.png[/img]

[h2]Employee Policies[/h2]
Currently, there are three different employee policies.

[b]Employee break policies[/b]
You can decide on when your employees go on breaks with employee break policies. 

[b]Employee parking policies[/b]
You can choose policies for the employees who own a car. They will only park in the employee parking spaces if you choose to but walking to work because all of the employee parking spaces are full will make them unhappy quickly.

[b]Employee locker policies[/b]
After you build employee locker rooms, you can set a policy to let them change into their uniforms at the casino hotel instead of at home. This will increase their job happiness.


So yes, your casino your rules! 
See you in the next post! Cheers!

notes.title: About CRT #9 | Maintenance
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/f6fae77337e70ce32d39a0f37115471c3ebb21e1.gif[/img]

We all know that the shiny new things you buy eventually break. It's one of the annoying things in life. Well, this rule also applies to the items in Casino Resort Tower. Every item has a maintenance value and the item breaks and becomes unusable if it's zero. You can sell it and buy a new one but it will be costly so repairing them regularly is the best option. 

Every room also has a maintenance value based on items it contains and this value affects your hotel rating. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/29afde8a690a9f6591e953f19038868a13b7d2e8.png[/img]


[h3]Maintenance People[/h3]
Repairs/maintenance can be done by maintenance officers. But it can be costly to hire maintenance officers if you are just starting. So if you have broken items and no budget you can always assign your CEO to do some repair work.

[h3]Maintenance Inventory[/h3]
To do repairs, people need to get tools from the maintenance office.
So always make sure you have some tools in the storage.



As always, feel free to contact us via Discord.
See you in the next post! Cheers!

notes.title: About CRT #7 | Waste Management
notes.content:
Hello everyone!
I know, we have 15 more topics to cover on About CRT before the EA launch and I'm kind of lagging behind. 
We are currently spending every waking hour on closed beta&demo but I will definitely create time to write the remaining posts.

So today's topic is waste management in Casino Resort Tower.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/496a6d9ffeff6556dc03ac854b33858d1fe94133.png[/img]

Almost anything related to the consumption of an inventory item or things like construction is going to create some waste. 
People in your casino hotel are going to use trash cans to dispose of it, but some of them are going to end up on the floor if your trash cans are full or you don't have them enough.

Full trash cans and trashes on the floor decrease the cleanliness value of the room and drop your hotel rating.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/945d2445c0a72e6e166ac3c5a1be505d9c6778cd.png[/img]

[h3]Trash Cans - Dumpsters[/h3]
Trash cans can be put around the hotel and used by your employees and customers. Dumpsters are placed in garbage rooms, and they are used by your janitors to put the trash they picked around your hotel while cleaning floors and emptying trash cans. Trash cans have a much lower capacity compared to dumpsters. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/4f564a83335594fdb60133e208dbcb8776077079.png[/img]

[h3]Janitors - Detergents&Garbage Bags[/h3]
Janitors get detergents and trash bags from janitorial rooms if you have them in your inventory first. After that, they collect trash by cleaning floors and emptying trash cans, then dump it into dumpsters you have in your garbage room if they have the available capacity.

[h3]Waste Collectors[/h3]
Waste collectors come every day to pick up trash from your dumpsters. And they leave after all of them is empty. They are not one of your employees, same as builders and delivery persons.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/e39244c58d4af3069c46163f7037371043e1b8c4.png[/img]

So yeah, this is the general logic behind it. 
Please let me know if you want to learn anything more specific.
And don't forget to join our discord to be part of the sweet community that we are building. 

I will see you in the next post, cheers!

notes.title: About CRT #6 | Research
notes.content:
Today's post is about the research system in Casino Resort Tower, so here we go.

Research documents are kind of a currency in CRT as I mentioned in the last post.  Every document can be produced by your CEO but if you want steady production of them, you will need offices. 

You can use research documents in events that we are going to cover in a future post. But the main and obvious usage is doing research.

There are 5 main research trees. So let's go through each one of them.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/3292240bf546a044184cd9a2216859dee9de75b5.png[/img]

[h3]Casino Research Tree[/h3]
You can research items like card tables, slot machines, dice tables, keno machines, bingo desks, etc. by casino research tree. But the important part is researching different kinds of games. Because every gambler has a favorite game and they will be extra happy if you have that game available.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/a3a1b5473f5a8d3fa55b355968ffe9caf49e0baa.png[/img]

[h3]Cuisine Research Tree[/h3]
You can research cafe services, restaurant services, bar services, vending machines, vendor services via cuisine research tree. You can also research menu items (snacks, appetizers, cocktails, main courses, tobacco products, hot drinks, cold drinks) to create delicious menus for your customers. We will also talk about managing your menus in a future post.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/35362402d07a5837c6081e9dbdc1fa73ce4f7685.png[/img]

[h3]Amenities Research Tree[/h3]
The amenities research tree is for researching casino hotel services like gym, gaming room, sauna, massage room, souvenir shop, meeting room, and the items needed for them. You know It's about the amenities part of a casino hotel. The amenities research tree also contains researches for different types of hotel rooms and items needed for them. From beds, wardrobes to minibars, nightstands, safe boxes. If you are creating a presidential hotel room it will need a lot. You can also research the facilities needed for a hotel service; laundry room, reception, and so on.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/3803a0955fdabaa641a24fb272f51ebcd0bfa30d.png[/img]

[h3]Building Research Tree[/h3]
Utilities, inventory, waste management, security. Facilities are the backstage services needed to run your casino hotel. So you can research everything related to it from this research tree. Anything related to transportation is also here. Transportation is about how people can come to your casino hotel. Taxi, bus, parking, metro services can be researched using this research tree so you can create spaces for transportation at your hotel's basement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/27b1524c2b474fde035dba6b401f0cb9ffd32a9a.png[/img]

[h3]Offices Research Tree[/h3]
The office research tree contains researches about HR, marketing, finance, research and CEO offices.
You can also research new marketing campaigns from here.


That's it for this post. I think the next one will be about waste management, then we will talk about offices a little more while going through finance and human resources.

Let me know in the comments or from the discord server if you want to hear something more specific.
Have an awesome day, cheers!

notes.title: About CRT #5 | Marketing
notes.content:
Hello! Today's post is about marketing in Casino Resort Tower.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/5be86b94b07391d0667a1b5cea70d2bd0dc34797.png[/img]

[h3]Marketing Campaigns[/h3]
You can start radio, flyer, podcast, social media, television marketing campaigns to create hype about your casino. More hype means more gamblers at your casino and that means more money. But be careful; if most of them leave your casino unhappy, your hotel rating will drop. You will have to correct things and wait for it to go back up or start a marketing campaign again.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/d304be406a8f637ec2b514c3d6b3de3c97ebca2d.png[/img]


[h3]Billboards[/h3]
You can also get advertisements to put around your casino to earn some extra money. You first need to put billboards around your hotel. That way you can get advertisement contracts from companies. These contracts demand a certain place like a lounge, bus stop, reception, and they also come with a deadline. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/a461ef7cdf4e620b97d1ea1e4e52f5791de99bc8.png[/img]


[h3]Marketing Documents[/h3]
To do anything related to marketing, you will need marketing documents. Documents are kind of a 'currency' in CRT that you can use while doing managerial things. There are currently four types of documents: Marketing, Accounting, Research, HR. We will talk about the other 3 of them in future posts.

Marketing documents are created by marketing specialists. So you need to build marketing offices with work desks, whiteboards, copiers and hire marketing specialists to create marketing documents for your archive.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/5a8221e502185afd6e7085b39403ae3fcae0c3fc.png[/img]


I guess this covers the general logic of marketing in CRT. Let me know in the comments if you want to hear something more specific.

Oh, there will be a closed beta soon. Join CRT Discord Server if you want to participate. 
https://discord.gg/2y5eXn3ubs

See you in the next one!

notes.title: About CRT #4 | Utilities
notes.content:
Hello hello!

We are working heavily on the demo so there were no posts in the last 2-3 weeks. I've planned around 20 posts to cover what mechanics/content will be available at the Early Access launch. And there is not much time left so I will post much more frequently from now on.

Anyways, today we are going to talk about utilities! 



There are currently 4 types of utility systems in CRT: Electricity, Water, Sewage, Internet. 
Each utility system has 3 parts: Producers, Consumers, Connectors.

Let's go through each one.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/de63e27616388e70a7196a098bbbdb945dd369be.png[/img]


[h2]System Parts[/h2]

[h3]Connectors[/h3]
Connectors are items like pipes, tubes, wires, and cables. They are used for, you guessed it, connecting producers and consumers. Every connector group forms utility lines. If a utility line exceeds a certain volume it will shut down. To prevent this you need to research high-capacity connectors with your research documents and replace them. Or you can also keep your utility lines separate by checking their volume.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/657f7d36f6e3561bac9b7029d9a01885f9c6cfe6.png[/img]

[h3]Producers[/h3]
Producers are items like water pumps, transformers, servers. They will produce the utility needs of your consumers.

[h3]Consumers[/h3]
Consumers are basically items that need a utility type(s) to function. It can be anything from a CCTV camera to a shower cabin.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/7ee5224e720012cefbb65667f7ed7584d3d55cf1.png[/img]


[h2]Utilility Types[/h2]

[h3]Electricity[/h3]
Electricity is the most commonly used utility type. Office desks, hand dryers, lamps, fridges; you know most of the items can't function without electricity. 

Producers: 
[list]
[*] Small Transformer
[*] Transformer
[*] Large Transformer
[/list]
Connectors: 
[list]

[*] High Capacity Wire
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/fb715343c0e01b6ee0dad1dbe6ba64b4c8cf2cbd.png[/img]

[h3]Sewage[/h3]
If there is water there is also sewage. Most of the items like shower cabins, dishwashers, toilet cabins, sinks use water but also need a sewage system to function properly.

Producers: 
[list]
[*] Small Sewage Pump
[*] Sewage Pump
[*] Large Sewage Pump
[/list]
Connectors: 
[list]
[*] Sewage Tube
[*] High Capacity Sewage Tube
[/list]


[h3]Water[/h3]
Water is mostly needed at spas, kitchens, restrooms.

Producers: 
[list]
[*] Small Water Pump
[*] Water Pump
[*] Large Water Pump
[/list]
Connectors:

[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/9564c6e48a0d07e71c8895e7b5e3866bf1b442b1.png[/img]

[h3]Internet[/h3]
Internet is generally used by offices with items like office desks, copiers.

Producers: 
[list]

[*] Server Rack
[*] Large Server Rack
[/list]
Connectors: 
[list]

[/list]




Yeap, that's it for now. Let me know in the comments if you want to hear something more specific.
Cheers!

notes.title: About CRT #3 | Inventory
notes.content:
Hey everyone, 

I thought it would be nice to talk about the inventory system in our third -About CRT- blog post so here we go.



Most of the customer services in CRT need supplies to function. So lots of customers mean high supply-demand.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/7be6a1d75f2f99bede77b8c6a9178acadb06f178.png[/img]

[h3]Usage[/h3]
Some of the inventory item consumers are:

[list]
[*] [b]Kitchens, Bars, Cafes:[/b] Once you add a new menu item to your menus people will start to order it. But every menu item needs different ingredients to be made by your staff. To give an example; a Cosmopolitan cocktail needs vodka, fruit juice, lemon to be made by a bartender, or a Macchiato coffee needs coffee beans and milk to be made by a barista.

[*] [b]Vending Machines:[/b] There are cigarette, beverage, coffee, snack vending machines you can place around the hotel in CRT. But for an item to be sold, it should be available in storage rooms.

[*] [b]Hotel Rooms:[/b] Some of the customers will stay in your hotel if you have hotel rooms. After they leave the hotel room, janitors and housekeepers will start the cleaning process. And they will need surface cleaners and laundry detergents to do so.

[*] [b]Maintenance Offices:[/b] Maintenance officers need tools to repair items around the hotel.

[*] [b]Souvenir Shops:[/b] If you want to sell items in your souvenir shop you will need to buy them first. 

[*] [b]Massage Rooms:[/b] Massage therapists consume massage oil for every customer they serve. 
[/list]

It will be too long if I go through every inventory item consumer here but this is the general logic of the usage of supplies. So when you expand the services of your casino hotel it will increase the consumption of supplies.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/b3083b21bb3b14a7e2d0fcf3484d029d2bfb8869.png[/img]

[h3]Delivery[/h3]
Inventory items that are bought will be delivered at 6 am every morning. Delivery persons will carry items to your storage rooms and place them on your shelves and fridges. Like builders, delivery persons are not one of your employees too so they will deliver items and leave. If you buy items or give auto-buy order after 6 am it will be delivered the next morning. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/dd42fca22188cde408d3e8d7d7569fca981501f0.png[/img]

[h3]Storage[/h3]
Some inventory items like fish, butter need fridges to be stored and others can be placed on a regular storage shelf. So after you assign a room as a storage room checking your hotel's order history and inventory item consumption is useful to decide what storage item to place.


So yeah, this is the general logic behind the inventory system in CRT. Let me know in the comments or Discord if you want to hear something more specific.

See you!

notes.title: About CRT #2 | Decoration & Lighting
notes.content:
Hello!


Today we will continue to talk about the build/design mechanics of the game. After these, we are going to go deep into management mechanics.

If you want to be a five-star casino hotel, decoration and lighting are two of the many necessary pieces.

But before explaining how decoration and lighting values change, I want to talk about tiles.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/6f9a1fad6d1dc495b3eb54b5326a3550f44f8cfe.png[/img]


[h3]Tiles[/h3]
In CRT; buildings contain floors, floors contain rooms, and rooms contain tiles. And these tiles hold some values like decoration, lighting, security, cleanliness.

Every tile affects the neighboring tiles if they are in the same room space. But if the neighbor tiles are separated by an interior wall, their values won't affect each other.

So when it comes to the casino hotel's total scores of decoration and lighting; It is an average of all of the room's scores, and the room's score is the average of the tiles it contains.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/3ec04be6682e03c152a2133ee74e04bc73d340d5.png[/img]


Decoration and lighting values change around the map by items and building improvements that are placed. 


[h3]Building Improvements[/h3]
When a wall is built, it's just concrete so it decreases the decoration of the room. Wallpapers look cool but they are also needed to make up for that. 

Windows and curtains can also be used while designing a room. Windows will increase both the decoration and lighting of the room. Curtains will increase decoration even more but it will decrease some of the lighting value of the tile.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/87ddcdb87503834ef02b2bff3f39d2a39de24cbf.png[/img]


[h3]Items[/h3]
There are lots of item types in CRT so we can't go through all of them here but to give some examples;

There are some obvious decoration increasers like statues, plants, paintings; and obvious lighting increasers like ceiling lamps, floor lamps. 
But a slot machine or an aquarium will increase the lighting value of a tile too.


Every item type also has different versions of them but the values are the same between versions, so you can use the one looks good for your taste.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/b1af4dec8087317294e5ff4403b0bf7b142e5f57.png[/img]


Item types like a sewage pump or a toilet cabin are necessary of course but they will decrease decoration moderately.




I don't want to make the posts too long to read but I hope this cleared some things about decoration and lighting.

I wish everyone a great day and hope to see you at the next post!

notes.title: About CRT #1 | Construction
notes.content:
Hello, hello!

I want to introduce the current mechanics of the Casino Resort Tower bit by bit until release. Then we will go to EA state and talk about updates, events, and plans.

Before we start, feel free to join our Discord server to be in the CRT community. Here is the link -> https://discord.gg/2y5eXn3ubs


So let's start with what every casino hotel starts. Yes, construction!

In CRT some objects need construction like walls, stairs, elevators. But players can place other objects directly like furniture, wallpapers, curtains, etc.

Today we are going to talk about the construction part of things. There are two types of walls and two types of floor connectors in CRT. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/30cd8457ff86745791a3b2a1e1edaae430f9a802.png[/img]


[list]
[*] [b]Infrastructure Wall[/b]: Used for increasing building space and creating floors.

[*] [b]Interior Wall[/b]: Used for separation to create spaces for rooms.

[*] [b]Stairs[/b]: Used for connecting neighboring floors. But Customers will complain if they want to go to Floor32 from Floor2 and the only way is the stairs.

[*] [b]Elevators[/b]: Used for connection multiple floors. Elevators are simulated (People are not teleporting from one elevator entrance to another; they are waiting for the cabin, getting in, etc.). So customers will complain if it is too slow or crowded. This can be prevented by increasing the elevator speed or capacity with research documents produced by the research office. (We will talk about office documents in detail at another post).
[/list]


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41717099/2ee0cafe4bab6e3290d156b2db445aab35dc13a8.png[/img]


[h3]Builders[/h3]
Let's continue with the builders. When an object with construction needs is placed, builders will come and start the construction. Builders are not one of your employees, they will come to do the job and go.


[h3]Stages[/h3]
Every construction has two stages. Builders will carry the necessary building materials to construction zones. Then they will start the construction and build the objects. 


[h3]Disturbance[/h3]
But be careful, if construction is too close to hotel rooms or massage rooms it will cause some disturbance. So it will be a wise decision to empty the neighboring rooms before the construction. 


[h3]Construction Trash[/h3]
Construction will also leave some trash after completion. We will go into garbage disposal mechanics in detail at another post.


So yeah, I think it's not bad and sums up some things for the first post. See you at the next one!
